Burkina/Solidarité : Plus 1,34 million de personnes retournées et accompagnées dans 1 055 localités
items.description: À l'occasion de la deuxième phase de la troisième édition des Journées nationales d'engagement patriotique et de participation citoyenne (JEPPC), la ministre de la Famille et de la Solidarité, Pélagie Kaboré, a présenté, le 5 octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou, les principales actions conduites par son département. Face aux représentants des forces vives, aux associations féminines ainsi qu'aux élèves et étudiants des structures de formation en travail social, elle a également décliné les priorités de son ministère pour renforcer la solidarité nationale et la protection des personnes vulnérables. La ministre de la Famille et de la Solidarité a présenté cette rencontre comme un moment de redevabilité, mais aussi comme une occasion d'écouter les préoccupations des populations et de recueillir leurs propositions. « Les résultats présentés aujourd'hui sont ceux d'un effort collectif », a-t-elle souligné. Elle estime que l'action publique doit rester au plus près des besoins des populations. Selon elle, son ministère inscrit son action dans les différents piliers du plan RELANCE 2026-2030, notamment ceux consacrés à la sécurité, à la cohésion sociale et à la paix, à la gouvernance ainsi qu'au développement du capital humain. Dans le domaine de l'action sociale, le département mise notamment sur des dispositifs destinés à faciliter l'accès des citoyens aux services sociaux. La plateforme numérique nationale « Deme Sira » permet ainsi aux citoyens de soumettre des requêtes d'assistance et de contribuer à l'effort national de solidarité. À cela s'ajoute le Service social mobile, lancé le 1ᵉʳ avril 2026 dans la région du Kadiogo, qui permet d'aller à la rencontre des personnes ayant des difficultés à accéder aux structures sociales classiques. Le Registre social unique (RSU) constitue également un outil important pour mieux cibler les interventions. À la date de la présentation, plus de 430 000 ménages y étaient enregistrés et bénéficiaient des interventions des acteurs humanitaires et de développement. Dans le domaine humanitaire, la ministre a fait état de résultats importants enregistrés au cours de la période considérée. Au 31 juillet 2026, le ministère dénombrait 1 346 769 personnes issues de 226 404 ménages retournées et accompagnées dans 1 055 localités. Au-delà de leur retour, les autorités cherchent à favoriser leur réinstallation durable à travers différents appuis aux moyens d'existence, notamment dans l'élevage, le maraîchage et la transformation des produits forestiers non ligneux. Des kits d'installation et des noyaux reproducteurs sont également mis à leur disposition. Par ailleurs, près de deux millions de personnes vulnérables ont bénéficié d'une assistance alimentaire. Pour renforcer les capacités opérationnelles du Conseil national de secours d'urgence et de réhabilitation (CONASUR), le ministère s'est également doté de 66 camions de ravitaillement humanitaire, destinés à faciliter l'acheminement de l'aide vers certaines localités. La ministre Pélagie Kaboré La protection des enfants constitue un autre axe majeur de l'action du ministère. Plus de 2 000 personnes en situation de mendicité ont été retirées des rues et prises en charge. De même, plus de 13 800 orphelins et enfants vulnérables, parmi lesquels des enfants de personnes tombées pour la patrie, ont bénéficié d'un appui à la scolarisation ou à la formation. La ministre a également indiqué que 1 330 pupilles de la Nation, ainsi que des milliers d'enfants victimes de violences, bénéficient d'une prise en charge adaptée. Celle-ci porte notamment sur l'état civil, la santé, l'alimentation, l'accompagnement psychosocial et l'insertion. La ministre a également mis en avant les actions en faveur de l'autonomisation économique des femmes. Près de 18 500 femmes ont bénéficié de crédits destinés au financement d'activités agro-pastorales. Des femmes déplacées internes et retournées ont, pour leur part, reçu des équipements et des appuis techniques pour développer leurs activités économiques. Elle a par ailleurs rappelé que les femmes survivantes de violences basées sur le genre bénéficient d'une prise en charge intégrée comprenant, selon leurs besoins, la protection, l'accompagnement psychosocial, l'orientation et le soutien à la réinsertion. Les produits présentés au cours de la rencontre, notamment les pagnes tissés Faso Dan Fani, les tenues Koko Dunda et les produits agroalimentaires, illustrent, selon la ministre, le savoir-faire des femmes, des personnes déplacées internes et des personnes retournées. Elle a ainsi appelé à faire de la consommation des produits locaux un véritable acte de souveraineté et de patriotisme économique. Selon le bilan présenté, plus de 1,2 million de personnes indigentes ont bénéficié d'une assistance psychosociale et sanitaire. Dans le même temps, plus de 28 000 personnes handicapées ont reçu un soutien adapté à leurs besoins. La production de cartes d'invalidité sécurisées participe également à l'amélioration de l'identification des personnes handicapées et à leur accès aux dispositifs prévus par la législation. La consolidation de la cohésion sociale constitue un autre volet important de l'action du ministère. À ce titre, 2 103 acteurs communautaires, dont 526 femmes, ont été renforcés sur les questions liées à la prévention et à la gestion des conflits sociaux, à la cohésion sociale ainsi qu'aux mécanismes traditionnels et endogènes de résolution des conflits. Ces acteurs comprennent notamment des représentants des chefferies coutumières et traditionnelles, des autorités religieuses, des organisations de la société civile, des leaders de personnes déplacées internes et des amazones de la cohésion sociale. Malgré les résultats enregistrés, la ministre reconnaît que les besoins restent importants. Elle a ainsi dégagé quatre grandes priorités pour les prochaines étapes de l'action de son département. Il s'agit d'abord de renforcer l'autonomisation économique et sociale des femmes et des filles, à travers le développement des capacités, le financement des initiatives productives et la promotion de leur participation à la vie économique et sociale. La deuxième priorité concerne le renforcement de la protection sociale et de l'inclusion des personnes vulnérables, notamment les enfants, les personnes handicapées, les personnes indigentes et les personnes confrontées à l'exclusion sociale. Le ministère entend également améliorer l'accessibilité des services sociaux, notamment grâce au développement des dispositifs de proximité et au renforcement des mécanismes d'identification, d'orientation et de prise en charge. Enfin, la restauration des moyens d'existence des personnes déplacées internes, retournées ou réinstallées, ainsi que des communautés hôtes vulnérables, devra se poursuivre afin de favoriser leur réinsertion socioéconomique, leur résilience et la consolidation de la cohésion sociale. En conclusion, la ministre a insisté sur la nécessité de poursuivre le dialogue avec les populations. Pour elle, rendre compte, c'est aussi écouter. La rencontre du 5 octobre aura ainsi permis de dresser le bilan des actions menées, mais aussi d'ouvrir la voie à de nouvelles propositions pour renforcer la protection sociale, l'autonomisation économique et la cohésion sociale au Burkina Faso. items.title: Rival clubs want range of punishments for Man City
items.description: A number of Premier League clubs want Manchester City to face both “retrospective punishments” and future sanctions for their mass financial rule-breaking, sources have told BBC Sport. An independent commission found City guilty of all charges relating to breaches of the Premier League’s financial regulations between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons. City have appealed against the verdict, while the Solicitors Regulation Authority (SRA) is poised to review the findings to determine whether there are any indications of potential misconduct. However, there is said to be a consensus among a group of top-flight club executives that if City’s appeal is unsuccessful, the sanctions should make reparations for the period when they broke the rules, while also limiting their powers in future. There is also a feeling from at least four Premier League boardrooms that a “one-hit” points deduction resulting in relegation to the Championship would be an insufficient punishment given the severity of City’s wrongdoing. There is an understanding that there is nuance in exactly what clubs consider a fitting penalty for the eight-time Premier League champions, who were found guilty of all serious financial rule breaches in a damning verdict by an independent commission. One senior club source said City should be stripped of their titles, and added there was “no great rush” among clubs to push for the redistribution of trophies, but rather to take honours away and leave them vacant. The source warned that the Premier League’s credibility would be lost if City were allowed to keep the eight major trophies they won during the period they were found guilty. However, in a sign of a range of opinions across the league, BBC Sport was previously told there was little appetite among other clubs for City to be stripped of titles. Regarding the timescale for future sanctions, there is concern among club executives that a sanction applied to just one season would merely provide City with a “bump in the road,” given the likelihood of their returning to the Premier League at the first opportunity. A number of Premier League figures therefore believe any points deduction should be split over multiple seasons, while there is also a sense that transfer bans spanning multiple windows would significantly hinder City’s ability to regain their top-flight status as quickly as possible. One club source also said it would be “bizarre, almost obtuse” if City were able to trade in the upcoming January transfer window, if this process is ongoing and sanctions have not been applied. Some clubs cited feeling “in the dark” regards the Premier League, including around the chronology and timescales of the appeal and the sanctions hearing. However, sources said there was “empathy” and “understanding” about the difficult position the Premier League is in, given the gravity of this situation and the ongoing legal process. Regarding financial reparations, one idea that has been mooted – and which a club source found “merit” in – was to apply a “tariff-based system”, whereby City’s past league finishing positions would be altered via a points deduction. Rival clubs could then be paid compensation by City based on where they would have finished versus where they did finish. BBC Sport understands that Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca will speak to players collectively after they return from international duty on Thursday, before their Premier League match against Liverpool on Sunday (16:30 BST). The trip to Anfield is their first game since the verdict was announced. Merseyside Police says it has received queries in relation to the match, and when asked by BBC Sport if any special measures would be put in place the force said it will have “an appropriate policing operation in place on the day”. Sources at Liverpool have told BBC Sport that it is a case of “business as usual” and that no extra measures are being put in place. Conversations and meetings between the club, supporters and relevant authorities take place before every home game. One source said while everyone “has the right to express their feelings” they hoped supporters would not overstep the mark.

items.title: Mamadi Doumbouya signe un décret portant attributions et organisation du ministère de la Défense Nationale
items.description: À travers un décret lu ce mardi soir sur les antennes de la télévision nationale, le président de la République a officiellement fixé les attributions et le cadre fonctionnel du ministère de la Défense Nationale. Revisitant les missions stratégiques, opérationnelles et administratives des forces armées, cette décision présidentielle clarifie la chaîne de commandement, renforce la gestion budgétaire et réaffirme l'ancrage institutionnel de la Défense au service de la nation et du développement socio-économique. ​ Synthèse des grands axes du décret ​Garantir et protéger les intérêts majeurs et vitaux de la nation ; ​Sauvegarder les institutions de la République ; ​Mettre en œuvre la politique de défense nationale ; ​Mettre en œuvre les décisions du Conseil Supérieur de la Défense Nationale (CSDN) ; ​Assurer l'organisation générale de la défense nationale ; ​Définir la politique d'audit et de contrôle des forces armées et en assurer la mise en œuvre ; ​Définir la politique de gestion prévisionnelle des ressources humaines et de la mobilisation des forces ; ​Définir les politiques de communication, du domaine et des infrastructures, de formation, de renseignement, de l’emploi des forces et de relations internationales de défense ; ​Exécuter les décisions du Président de la République, Commandant en chef suprême des forces armées, notamment celles concernant l'avancement, la mise à la retraite du personnel des forces de défense, la nomination aux emplois de commandement et les déplacements des unités constituées hors de leur garnison ; ​Coordonner les activités des organismes de commandement ; ​Assurer la mise en condition des forces ; ​Faire participer les forces armées au développement socio-économique du pays et à toute autre tâche d'intérêt public ; ​Élaborer les directives générales pour les négociations en matière de défense ; ​Assurer la tutelle des anciens combattants et victimes de guerre ; ​Gérer le patrimoine militaire ; ​Créer et renforcer les conditions de participation des forces aux missions de soutien de la paix ; ​Faire observer les principes du droit international humanitaire et des droits de l'homme au sein des forces armées. ​Sous l'autorité du Président de la République, le ministère de la Défense nationale est dirigé par un officier général ou un cadre civil en activité ou à la retraite. Le ministre en charge de la Défense nationale assure la tutelle politique et administrative de l'institution militaire. Il a autorité sur l'ensemble des forces armées. Sur la conduite des actions courantes, aussi bien dans le domaine opérationnel que dans le domaine administratif, il peut déléguer par arrêté une partie de ses pouvoirs à ses grands subordonnés. Le ministre en charge de la Défense nationale est l'ordonnateur du budget de la Défense nationale ; à ce titre, il peut désigner des ordonnateurs délégués sous l'exécution dudit budget.

items.title: Eau minérale en Guinée : le ministère du Commerce fixe de nouveaux prix plafonds applicables dès le 7 octobre
items.description: Le ministère de l’Industrie et du Commerce a annoncé, ce mardi 6 octobre 2026, une nouvelle grille de prix plafonds pour l’eau minérale et minéralisée conditionnée, applicable sur l’ensemble du territoire national à compter du mercredi 7 octobre. Cette décision intervient à l’issue d’une rencontre de concertation tenue le lundi 5 octobre entre les services techniques du département et les différents acteurs de la filière. Les échanges ont notamment porté sur la structure des coûts et les conditions de commercialisation de l’eau conditionnée. Selon la nouvelle tarification annoncée à la télévision nationale, les bouteilles de 33 à 35 centilitres, conditionnées par paquet de 15, sont plafonnées à 20 000 GNF à la sortie usine, 22 000 GNF chez le grossiste et 25 000 GNF au détail. La même grille tarifaire s’applique aux bouteilles de 50 à 55 centilitres, vendues par paquet de 12, ainsi qu’aux bouteilles de 1,5 litre, conditionnées par paquet de 6. Pour les bonbonnes de 19 litres, le prix plafond est fixé à 15 000 GNF à la sortie usine, 17 000 GNF chez le grossiste et 20 000 GNF au détail. La consigne de la bonbonne fixée à 50 000 GNF Le ministère précise également que la consigne de la bonbonne de 19 litres est fixée à 50 000 GNF. Cette somme ne doit être perçue qu’une seule fois, lors de la première acquisition de la bonbonne. Elle devra être intégralement remboursée au client lorsque celle-ci est restituée en bon état. Par ailleurs, les opérateurs de la filière sont désormais tenus d’afficher clairement les prix à chaque étape de la commercialisation. Toute opération de vente en gros doit être accompagnée d’une facture mentionnant notamment le produit concerné, son conditionnement et le prix appliqué. Le département du Commerce rappelle également qu’aucun opérateur ne peut refuser de vendre aux prix plafonds convenus dans le cadre de cette nouvelle grille tarifaire. Le ministre de l’Industrie et du Commerce, Aboubacar Kourouma, appelle ainsi l’ensemble des acteurs de la filière au strict respect des nouveaux prix. Les consommateurs sont, de leur côté, invités à signaler toute violation de ces dispositions ou toute pratique abusive auprès des services compétents, à travers le numéro vert 142. La nouvelle tarification entre officiellement en vigueur à partir du 7 octobre 2026. items.title: Emploi, investissements et eau : le PDG de la Société Hamana alerte sur les défis du secteur privé en Guinée
items.description: L’opérateur économique Mohamed Kourouma, PDG de la Société HAMANA, a animé ce mardi 6 octobre 2026 une conférence de presse à Conakry, au cours de laquelle il s’est exprimé sur plusieurs enjeux économiques, notamment l’emploi, l’investissement privé et les difficultés d’approvisionnement en eau conditionnée depuis l’interdiction des sachets plastiques à usage unique. Sur la question de l’emploi, Mohamed Kourouma estime que le déficit d’investissements privés constitue l’une des principales causes du manque d’opportunités, particulièrement pour les jeunes. Selon lui, l’amélioration du climat des affaires et la stabilité restent indispensables pour attirer les investisseurs. « Dès qu’un pays traverse des difficultés, de la tension ou de l’instabilité, les investisseurs ne viennent jamais. Chez nous, on peut toujours pratiquer le petit commerce informel, mais créer des usines, développer l’agriculture, l’élevage ou de grands projets d’entreprise, c’est impossible sans stabilité. C’est là le véritable problème de la Guinée », a-t-il déclaré. Le PDG de HAMANA a également insisté sur la nécessité de mieux définir le rôle de l’État et celui du secteur privé dans l’économie. « Penser que l’État doit tout prendre en charge relevait de l’époque du modèle communiste, où tout appartenait à l’État. Aujourd’hui, les règles économiques ont changé : l’État perçoit les taxes, les droits de douane et les impôts, mais ce n’est pas lui qui gère directement la production industrielle ou agricole », a-t-il soutenu. Pour illustrer les conséquences de la faiblesse du secteur privé sur l’emploi, Mohamed Kourouma a évoqué l’absence de grandes unités industrielles dans plusieurs régions du pays. « Les entreprises privées qui devraient s’installer et créer des usines à Kindia, Mamou, Kankan, en Guinée forestière ou à Labé ne sont pas là. Résultat : seul l’État fonctionne. Or, si seul l’État emploie et que le secteur privé est absent, il ne peut pas y avoir assez d’emplois pour la jeunesse », a-t-il alerté. L’opérateur économique estime que le développement de la Guinée passe nécessairement par une plus grande implication du secteur privé. Il cite notamment l’exemple de plusieurs pays européens et américains qui, selon lui, ont bâti leur économie sur l’industrie, l’agriculture et l’entrepreneuriat, parfois en dépit de ressources minières limitées. « En Europe ou en Amérique, c’est le secteur privé qui dynamise l’économie. Certains pays européens n’ont même pas de bauxite ni de ressources minières, mais ils se sont développés grâce à l’industrie, l’agriculture et l’entrepreneuriat. C’est grâce à cela qu’ils ont enrichi leurs nations. Chez nous, on continue de tout attendre de l’État », a-t-il fait remarquer. Il a également appelé à préserver un climat politique et social propice aux investissements. « Tant qu’un pays connaît la division, le communautarisme ou le conflit, les investisseurs ne viendront pas. Et s’ils ne viennent pas, ce sont les citoyens qui en souffrent », a-t-il prévenu. La crise de l’eau conditionnée Au cours de la même conférence de presse, Mohamed Kourouma s’est prononcé sur les difficultés d’approvisionnement en eau conditionnée apparues depuis l’entrée en vigueur, le 21 septembre, de l’interdiction des sachets plastiques à usage unique. Le patron de HAMANA estime que la situation actuelle s’explique principalement par le décalage entre la demande et les capacités de production de bouteilles d’eau. Il a toutefois salué l’adhésion de la population à la nouvelle réglementation, soulignant la disparition rapide de l’eau en sachet après l’entrée en vigueur de l’interdiction. « Il faut féliciter la population guinéenne. Depuis l’interdiction de l’utilisation des sachets plastiques à usage unique, l’eau en sachet a disparu en trois jours. Cela veut dire que le Guinéen a commencé à comprendre qu’il faut respecter la loi », a-t-il déclaré. Selon Mohamed Kourouma, l’ampleur des difficultés actuelles s’explique par le poids qu’occupait l’eau en sachet dans les habitudes de consommation. « En Guinée, ce sont les sachets et les bouteilles qui sont utilisés pour la consommation d’eau. 85 % de la population utilisaient l’eau en sachet et 15 % les bouteilles d’eau. Avec l’interdiction des plastiques à usage unique, les sachets d’eau ont disparu. Maintenant, les 15 % de bouteilles d’eau qui sont sur le marché ne suffisent pas à satisfaire toute la population. C’est pour cela qu’il y a eu une crise d’eau », a expliqué le PDG de HAMANA. Pour lui, l’augmentation des capacités de production ne peut cependant pas être immédiate. Les producteurs doivent adapter leurs installations à une demande qui a fortement augmenté depuis la disparition des sachets. « Pour produire 100 % de bouteilles d’eau, ça va prendre du temps. C’est la difficulté qu’il y a en ce moment. Il faut se dire la vérité. Maintenant, je pense que l’État est là pour aider la population, il n’est pas là pour la fatiguer. L’État est en train d’étudier. Je pense qu’ils vont trouver la solution », a-t-il conclu. À travers ses différentes interventions, Mohamed Kourouma a ainsi plaidé pour un renforcement du secteur privé et un environnement plus favorable aux investissements, tout en appelant à accompagner les entreprises confrontées aux conséquences de nouvelles mesures réglementaires.

items.title: Tear gas in Paris and Marseille as school protests grow across France
items.description: Hundreds of thousands of people have taken to the streets across France, as a wave of protests by high-school pupils spread to their parents, university students and unions. Crowds of teenagers marched from the Place de la République in Paris, calling for more resources for schools, and what they called less repression from police. Police clashed with demonstrators in Lyon, used tear gas in Paris and Marseille and water cannon in Rennes, but there was little of the serious trouble that marred previous protests. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu condemned the earlier violence and said since the protests had begun, 215 students and 85 staff had been hurt, as well as 715 police officers. The government said there had been disruptions in 891 high schools on Tuesday, almost a quarter of all lycées , and that more than 250,000 demonstrators had taken to the streets during the day. Students’ unions put the number at 450,000, and said the number of high schools blockaded was 1,800 on what the protesters dubbed “Act Three” of their movement. In Marseille, thousands of demonstrators moved around this city, stopping momentarily to chant before moving on as police changed direction. A group of masked protesters grabbed bollards and bins and tried to barricade themselves off from police. Riot officers fired tear gas, and the protesters dispersed. “Most of us aren’t violent,” said Alissa, a student in Marseille. “We’re going to the streets because they’ve closed our schools… schools are falling apart.” Her friend, Sacha, said the ceilings in Marseille’s schools were leaking and conditions were generally rather poor, “so we can’t really work a lot of time”. “We will keep doing this until good measures are taken,” he added. In parliament, the prime minister accused the radical-left France Unbowed (LFI) party of seeking to “sow chaos” ahead of presidential elections in seven months’ time. President Emmanuel Macron is nearing the end of his second and final term in office, and LFI leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon is currently runner-up in the opinion polls behind Marine Le Pen of the hard-right National Rally. Macron was due to chair a meeting with ministers at the Élysée Palace on Tuesday evening to assess the situation. Education Minister Édouard Geffray said that from the start he had appealed for dialogue rather than school blockades and complained that “ultra-violent elements infiltrated the high-school student movements”. He is now under pressure to respond to the students’ demands. What has been offered, including a website for students to express their grievances and an afternoon of internal discussion in schools on Friday, has made little impression so far. There seems little chance of the protests coming to an end just yet. France’s biggest union, the CGT, has said that further protests involving school and university students are being planned for Thursday. The protests began in mid-September but have spread to high schools across France There is widespread concern over allegations of “disproportionate force” by police, and France’s IGPN police inspectorate has been investigating a number of cases. One police officer who fired a tear-gas grenade at a high school student at Saint-Ouen-l’Aumône, north-west of Paris, last week has now been charged by prosecutors with “violence… resulting in mutilation or permanent disability”. Eden, 14, was part of a group blockading the Château d’Épluches lycée for 15-18-year-olds when he was hit in the face. His lawyer said he suffered a fractured jaw, and that his upper teeth were broken and four of his lower teeth were gone. On Monday, a 15-year-old’s hand was torn off after a so-called anti-encirclement grenade was fired in unclear circumstances near a school in the northern city of Lens. Authorities say he picked up the “sting ball” grenade which then exploded, but students allege he was hit directly after an officer fired. The grenade is considered a non-lethal weapon and the local prefect has said the incident took place when police were confronted by a group of 200-250 students throwing stones and fireworks. What began with local anger at overcrowded classrooms, a lack of teaching staff and dilapidated school buildings in the northern Paris suburb of Seine-Saint-Denis in mid-September has since spread across the country, and extended to some universities too. Late on Tuesday, the French interior ministry said a total of 6,547 had been stopped or arrested by police since 28 September. Tuesday’s protests drew people of all ages. One couple in their 70s, Alain and Michèle, joined the march in central Paris, to show their support for young students, explaining that as former teachers they understood the problems that France’s education system was facing. “We are the grandparents of three students who are all mobilised. They have protested peacefully in front of their respective high schools in Paris in recent days, but they were still tear-gassed,” Alain told the BBC, his voice trembling.

items.title: Kane inspires England to win over Czech Republic in UEFA Nations League
items.description: Harry Kane celebrated his record-equalling 125th England cap with two goals in a comfortable UEFA Nations League victory against the Czech Republic at Wembley. Kane made it a remarkable tally of 91 goals for England on the night he drew level with Peter Shilton – and is now firmly on course to become the first player to reach a century for his country. England built on the win against the Czech Republic in Prague and the outstanding 7-0 victory in Croatia with another convincing display to delight head coach Thomas Tuchel and the home support. Kane had a hand in England’s opener after 27 minutes, when his cross was turned into his own net by former West Ham United defender Vladimir Coufal. The goal Kane and Wembley craved came five minutes before the break, England’s captain applying a simple close-range finish to Morgan Rogers’ excellent first-time delivery. And Kane was on target again after 57 minutes, rising at the far post to head home Lewis Hall’s corner. Kane departed to a well-deserved standing ovation when he was replaced by Dominic Calvert-Lewin in the closing minutes. England show signs of progress England’s Uefa Nations League campaign may have started with defeat against World Cup holders Spain at Wembley but three subsequent victories, all achieved in convincing fashion, hinted at progress and optimism. Indeed, it could have been four wins from four had Kane scored the penalty that would have put England 3-1 up against Spain before the lost 3-2, but head coach Tuchel will have been highly satisfied with what he has seen since. England, after winning 7-0 in Croatia, were a threat again against the Czechs at Wembley, although Eberechi Eze failed to make the most of his opportunity with in-form Anthony Gordon rested. Tuchel’s attacking force is now set in stone, led by captain Harry Kane, with Gordon and Bukayo Saka on either side and Jude Bellingham stamping his world-class in the number 10 position. Trent Alexander-Arnold took his chance at right-back after being recalled by Tuchel following his World Cup exclusion, looking solid in defence – albeit not under huge pressure – while offering an extra dimension in attack. Newcastle United’s Hall now has strong claims to be first-choice left-back, while Jarell Quansah impressed with his versatility at right-back then in central defence against the Czechs, cementing his place as a vital part of Tuchel’s squad. England face Croatia next in November before their biggest test, away to Spain, but they have foundations to build on. And it was fitting that Kane marked the night when he equalled that caps record with two goals, capping a pleasing international break for Tuchel and England.

items.title: France/Lycéens : le PS va déposer une proposition de loi contre les armes mutilantes
items.description: Le chef des députés socialistes à l'Assemblée, Boris Vallaud, a annoncé mardi que son groupe allait déposer une proposition de loi pour que face à des manifestations impliquant des mineurs, les forces de l'ordre ne puissent plus utiliser d'armes mutilantes ou de « pratiques brutales ». « Nous déposerons une proposition de loi pour que lorsqu'il s'agit de manifestations lycéennes, avec une majorité de mineurs (…), il n'y ait pas d'utilisation de grenades de désencerclement, de LBD (lanceur de balle de défense, NDLR) ou de pratiques brutales comme l'étranglement », a expliqué le député des Landes sur RMC. Alors que le mouvement lycéen, accompagné de nombreuses violences, ne faiblit pas, plusieurs jeunes ont été blessés à la suite d'interventions des forces de l'ordre. Un lycéen de 15 ans a notamment eu la main arrachée par une grenade policière lundi à Lens. Dix enquêtes ont été ouvertes par l'inspection générale de la police nationale depuis le début du mouvement mi-septembre. Rappelant que parmi les jeunes interpellés, « 85% » étaient mineurs, Boris Vallaud a réclamé « une réponse d'abord éducative ». Or, a-t-il observé, « la cellule de crise face au mouvement des lycéens s'organise place Beauvau et pas rue de Grenelle », c'est-à-dire au ministère de l'Intérieur et non à celui de de l'Éducation. Parallèlement à cette initiative parlementaire, une pétition a été déposée sur le site de l'Assemblée nationale contre « une réponse sécuritaire totalement disproportionnée ». Les quelque 8.000 premiers signataires y demandent « l'interdiction des gestes d'immobilisation à risque d'asphyxie: plaquage ventral (maintien au sol sur le ventre avec compression thoracique), clés d'étranglement (prises au cou bloquant la respiration ou la circulation sanguine), pliage corporel (compression du buste vers les genoux) ». Ils réclament également « le retrait des armes mutilantes comme les LBD 40, les grenades explosives et de désencerclement » et « les pistolets à impulsion électrique (Taser) ». Laurent Nuñez avait indiqué ces derniers jours sur TF1 qu'il n'y avait « aucune consigne de retenue (en direction des forces de l'ordre) et aucune consigne de ne pas utiliser tout l'armement intermédiaire à disposition ». « Quand vous voyez des policiers harnachés comme s'il y avait une guerre (…). Comment est-ce qu'un ministre de l'Intérieur a pu perdre autant la maîtrise de la doctrine du maintien de l'ordre ? », s'est interrogée la candidate à la primaire sociale-démocrate Ségolène Royal (PS) sur franceinfo. The post France/Lycéens : le PS va déposer une proposition de loi contre les armes mutilantes appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Finland orders halt to work on two Google data centres
items.description: Finnish authorities have ordered a halt to building work at two planned Google data centres amid concerns over the clearance of more than 300 hectares of forest. The sites form part of Google’s record €13bn (£11bn; $15bn) investment in Finland, announced less than a month ago and described by the company as its largest single investment in Europe. The Finnish Supervisory Agency (LVV) said work at one site was carried out without a mandatory environmental impact assessment and ordered measures that would “significantly alter the environment” to be suspended by 23 October. Google said it had “fallen short of our own high standards in this instance” and would follow the agency’s guidance. The orders relate to preparatory work carried out at the planned data centre sites in Muhos and Kajaani. According to LVV’s head of environment Tommi Muilu, work at the sites included the removal of trees and topsoil, the construction of site roads and storage areas, and changes to ditches. Tuike Finland, the company behind Google’s data centre projects, has been asked to provide an explanation and set out how it intends to proceed by 14 October. The agency said it could begin “enforcement proceedings” if the company failed to comply with its demand. Hanna Halmeenpaa, chair of the Finnish Association for Nature Conservation, had previously told the AFP news agency that “nature sites which should be preserved” had been felled. The conservation group had previously called for work to be halted while the environmental requirements were examined. In a statement to the BBC, Google said: “We understand the concerns and have fallen short of our own high standards in this instance.” It said it had “acted in good faith under the Forestry Act”, carried out nature surveys and put measures in place to protect areas of high environmental value. “As we continue our long-term work in the region, we are advancing our landscaping and biodiversity plans, which include tree planting across 130 hectares at Muhos,” the company added. Google announced last month that it would invest at least €13bn (£11bn; $15bn) in Finland over 2027 and 2028. Its plans included new data centres in Kajaani, Muhos and Vaala, alongside investment in its existing facility in Hamina. The company said the infrastructure would help it meet growing demand for services including Search, Maps and its AI assistant Gemini. Google said the construction phase in 2027 and 2028 would support more than 37,000 jobs and contribute an average of €3.6bn a year to Finland’s economy. As part of its expansion, Google also signed a 22-year power purchasing agreement with Finnish energy company Fortum covering up to half the capacity of the Loviisa nuclear power plant. Fortum said the agreement would help support the plant’s continued operation until 2050. Finland has attracted growing interest in data centres, with its cool climate and low-carbon electricity among the factors making it attractive to developers. Lower temperatures can also reduce the energy required to cool facilities filled with computer servers.

items.title: Substitute Merino scores twice as Spain win in Croatia
items.description: Arsenal midfielder Mikel Merino came off the bench to score twice as world champions Spain fought back from a goal down to beat Croatia in the Nations League and reach the quarter-finals. Coach Luis de la Fuente’s Spain went into this game looking to record their 11th consecutive win, but they fell behind in the 17th minute when Ivan Perisic headed in. Croatia had been thrashed 7-0 by England in their previous Nations League fixture but were given a standing ovation at half-time in this game following a much-improved display. However, Spain were stronger after the break and drew level in the 61st minute when Dani Olmo got onto a poor clearance and picked out Merino, who made no mistake. Lamine Yamal saw a goalbound shot blocked as Spain pushed for the winner, before Perisic was sent off for Croatia just moments after seeing a strong effort saved. The 37-year-old was shown a second yellow for a foul on Marc Cucurella. That dismissal perhaps proved costly, and Spain snatched the three points two minutes from time when Merino latched onto a fine ball from Arsenal teammate Martin Zubimendi before sending a brilliant finish into the back of the net. Spain are top of League A – Group 3, three points ahead of England who comfortably beat the Czech Republic 3-0 on Tuesday.

items.title: Eau minérale : de nouveaux prix plafonds fixés à compter du 7 octobre
items.description: Le ministère de l’Industrie et du Commerce a annoncé, ce mardi 6 octobre 2026, de nouveaux prix plafonds pour l’eau minérale et minéralisée conditionnée sur l’ensemble du territoire national. Le communiqué, lu à la télévision nationale, fait suite à une rencontre de concertation tenue le 5 octobre entre les services techniques du ministère et les acteurs de la filière. À l’issue des échanges consacrés notamment à la structure des coûts, les parties ont convenu d’une nouvelle grille tarifaire applicable à partir du 7 octobre 2026. Pour les bouteilles de 33 à 35 cl, vendues par paquet de 15, le prix plafond est fixé à 20 000 GNF à la sortie usine, 22 000 GNF chez le grossiste et 25 000 GNF au détail. La même grille s’applique aux bouteilles de 50 à 55 cl par paquet de 12 ainsi qu’aux bouteilles de 1,5 litre par paquet de 6. Concernant les bonbonnes de 19 litres, le prix plafond est établi à 15 000 GNF à la sortie usine, 17 000 GNF chez le grossiste et 20 000 GNF au détail. Le ministère précise également que la consigne de la bonbonne de 19 litres est fixée à 50 000 GNF. Cette somme n’est perçue qu’une seule fois lors de la première acquisition et doit être intégralement remboursée lorsque la bonbonne est restituée en bon état. Les opérateurs sont par ailleurs tenus d’afficher les prix à chaque étape de la commercialisation. Toute vente en gros doit être accompagnée d’une facture précisant le produit, son conditionnement et le prix appliqué. Le ministère rappelle également qu’aucun opérateur ne peut refuser de vendre aux prix plafonds convenus. Le ministre de l’Industrie et du Commerce, Aboubacar Kourouma, appelle ainsi les acteurs de la filière au strict respect de cette nouvelle tarification. Les consommateurs sont, pour leur part, invités à signaler toute violation ou pratique abusive auprès des services compétents, via le numéro vert 142.

items.title: Ronaldo wants Portugal ‘punishment’ but not retiring
items.description: Cristiano Ronaldo says he is not retiring from international football but deserves to be punished for walking out on Portugal after head coach Jorge Jesus twice “broke his word”. The 41-year-old captain left his country’s Nations League camp last week after being an unused substitute against Norway and learning he would not start against Denmark. Al-Nassr forward Ronaldo has scored 146 goals in 234 Portugal appearances, both world records, helping them win Euro 2016 and the Nations League twice. In a lengthy statement which ran to nearly 2,000 words, the former Real Madrid and Manchester United player said he should be held accountable for his actions. But he accused Jesus of an “absolute breach of trust” for first not playing him against Norway after saying he would, and then going back on his decision to present an agreed version of events to the media. “The Portuguese Football Federation must assess the consequences of my actions and punish me for them. I believe the punishment should not be reduced,” Ronaldo said. “I have already apologised, but I know that actions have consequences.” Ronaldo’s statement comes after Portugal head coach Jesus said there was no rift with the captain, following claims the five-time Ballon d’Or winner had refused to train. What does Ronaldo say happened? Ronaldo’s statement struck a conciliatory tone in places, but he was also critical of Portugal coach Jesus as he provided his version of the dispute which prompted him to walk out on the squad last week. He said Jesus had agreed a plan under which the forward would miss the Norway and Denmark matches to manage his fitness. However, on the day of the Norway game, the 72-year-old coach told him he would play for 30 minutes. “Everyone knows the rest. I warmed up from half-time onwards, watched the minutes tick by and wasn’t called on,” Ronaldo said. “The manager had broken his word to me.” A later meeting with Jesus produced an agreement for the coach to clarify matters at his next news conference. Ronaldo said an eight-point document was prepared saying he had never demanded playing time, had respected Jesus’ decisions and that the coach asking “someone of the stature of Pele or Maradona” to warm up without bringing him on had been a mistake. Portugal’s record appearance holder said the agreed notes did not require Jesus to apologise to him but said the coach’s public remarks did not reflect their private discussion. “The conference was what is known: the attitude had nothing to do with our meeting,” Ronaldo explained. “I heard expressions and an aggressiveness I believe I did not deserve, a “High and mighty” attitude that he never showed me, not even remotely, in private the day before.” Ronaldo said it was the “second time” Jesus had “broken his word to me” and he decided to leave the training camp “without waiting for any further broken promises”. Prior to his appointment as head coach, Ronaldo said he had described Jesus – who had previously managed him at Al Nassr – as the “right choice”. Ronaldo had considered retiring from international football after this summer’s World Cup – at which Portugal exited at the last-16 stage – and said he had written a letter to fans containing the words he wanted to tell them when he announced it, but he was urged to reconsider by the FPF’s president, Pedro Proenca, on the flight home from the United States. Ronaldo’s behaviour drew contrasting opinions in his homeland with Jesus getting some support in the media and among fans at odds with those loyal to legendary player. Ronaldo said that, despite the “absolute breakdown of trust” in Jesus’ word, he should not have left and the “responsibility is mine alone”, as he said sorry to his fellow players and Portugal’s supporters. He added: “I owe an apology to my national team teammates for having left the camp… I apologise to the Portuguese people once again, but a broken word has, for me, a defining impact.” Jesus said on Sunday that the door was still open for Ronaldo to play for the country’s national team. Ronaldo said that, provided he was “physically fit, playing with my team, and hopefully scoring goals”, he would like to continue to play international football. “After my suspension period ends, I will be available, as I always have been, to compete and win with our national team,” he added. BBC Sport has approached the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) for comment.

items.title: Barack Obama Looks Left
items.description: This is an edition of The Atlantic Daily, a newsletter that guides you through the biggest stories of the day, helps you discover new ideas, and recommends the best in culture. Sign up for it here. The Democratic Party needs Abdul El-Sayed, but it doesn’t necessarily love him. Although few top Democrats have expressed public misgivings about El-Sayed, the leftist candidate for U.S. Senate in Michigan who defeated an establishment candidate in an August primary, most of them aren’t overflowing with enthusiasm either. This hesitation is one reason yesterday’s news that former President Obama will campaign with El-Sayed and other Michigan Democrats later this month is notable. Seeing why El-Sayed would want Obama’s imprimatur is easy: He’s by far the most popular politician in America, and he won Michigan in both of his presidential races—once by more than 16 percentage points and another by nearly 10, over a native Michigander. (More unexpected is El-Sayed’s welcome for Kamala Harris, who is unpopular with leftists, lost Michigan in 2024, and has gotten a stiff arm from some Democratic candidates this cycle.) Obama’s incentives are more interesting. He is in an awkward phase of his career—no longer young enough to be cool but still too young to be an elder statesman. Nonetheless, with Bill Clinton and Joe Biden both aging and somewhat tarnished, no other figure can match Obama’s stature. He has become, as Politico put it today , the Democratic Party’s “closer-in-chief.” In that role, he’s been more willing to back left-wing candidates than other establishment figures have. Last year, many high-profile Democrats were wary of the New York mayoral candidate Zohran Mamdani—either because they were skeptical of his policy stances or because of their long-standing ties to the family of his leading opponent, Andrew Cuomo. But Obama privately called him , praised his campaign, and offered to be a “sounding board” should Mamdani want advice. (Obama did not formally endorse Mamdani, though The New York Times , which first reported the call, noted that he prefers not to intervene in municipal races.) And in 2018, Obama endorsed Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for U.S. House. He did so only after she’d won a primary in a safe district, so the outcome was a foregone conclusion, but given her anti-establishment campaign, he seemed to be sending a message —or placing a bet on future success. (Obama also privately called El-Sayed after his primary victory.) Obama’s engagement with leftist candidates stands in contrast with most of his statements on leftist politics. Ideologically, Obama’s stances remain essentially center-left—even as the party overall has shifted leftward since he departed the White House —and he has at times appeared to scold or at least push back on the party’s left wing. Since leaving office, he has criticized cancel culture , slogans such as “Defund the police,” and what he views as a culture of ideological purity . Some critics on the left have been happy to return fire, labeling him a fake progressive who is too cozy with the powerful . Notwithstanding his overall popularity, Obama has drawn grumbling from other parts of the party, too. Some critics complain that he spends too much time jetting around the globe, hobnobbing with NBA stars, and podcasting with Bruce Springsteen. Even his year-end playlists and reading lists feel a bit stale. (Obama bristled when the comedian Hasan Minhaj questioned whether he really made them.) In good times, this would be merely cringe; in a time of rising authoritarianism, some view him not being more actively involved in politics as a dereliction of duty. Obama tends to lock in for campaign season, and he is a consummate party man; if the Democrats need to win the Michigan Senate seat, Obama will hit the stump for the nominee, whomever that might be. But Obama may have other reasons to embrace candidates such as El-Sayed and Mamdani. The politician who once described himself as a “skinny kid with a funny name” may see some of the same in them—or, in El-Sayed’s case, a swole kid. He is not a Muslim, as they are, but he was a target of Islamophobic attacks . And he is not a leftist, like them, but he was often tarred as a radical socialist. Beyond the personal, Obama has signaled some impatience with more traditional elements of the Democratic Party during appearances in the past two years, echoing the boisterous left more than the buttoned-up establishment. He has criticized what he sees as faintheartedness from Democrats who he said last year were “cowed and intimidated and shrinking away from just asserting what they believe, or at least what they said they believe.” In sidestepping internecine battles, he has also suggested agnosticism about methods as long as the results are good. “There’s been, I gather, some argument between the left of the party and people who are promoting the quote-unquote abundance agenda. Listen, those things are not contradictory. You want to deliver for people and make their lives better? You got to figure out how to do it,” he said . Obama will never have the same policy slate as Senator Bernie Sanders or Zohran Mamdani do, but his rhetoric and backing of leftist candidates suggest that he’s more attuned to shifts in the Democratic Party than his establishment peers are, and less rigid than his leftist critics contend. In 2008, Obama promised change; in 2026, he is still willing to give it a shot. Related: Where is Barack Obama? The firebrand Here are three new stories from The Atlantic : Tom Nichols: Russia needs to tell the truth about a plague death. The battle for Hormuz is not the war. What Justice Alito really wants Today’s News Cornell’s faculty introduced a no-confidence resolution over the university’s handling of an alleged 2024 sexual assault at a fraternity house. The faculty senate is expected to consider the measure on October 14 amid calls for changes to how the university addresses sexual assault. Paramount completed its $81 billion takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery , creating a new media giant called Skydance. The combined company brings HBO, CNN, CBS, Paramount, and their major film and streaming franchises under one owner. Student-led protests in France over poor school conditions spread to more than 40 cities , drawing roughly 256,000 people, including teachers, parents, and unions. The government suspended classes for two days as the movement grew, and some protests ended in clashes with police. Evening Read Jeff Blake / The Washington Post / Getty Churches Are Finally Making the Moral Case Against Sports Betting By McKay Coppins One of the puzzling things about the online sports-betting boom that has swept through American culture over the past decade is the relative slowness of religious leaders to articulate a moral case against the vice. In the past, churches were among the leading voices warning against gambling. Jerry Falwell denounced it as a sinful habit that preyed on the poor and left “little children” to pay the price. In The Atlantic ’s December 1907 issue, a Unitarian minister made the case against “speculation.” “The long and costly experience of mankind bears uniform testimony against gambling,” Charles F. Dole wrote . “It is a dangerous or unsocial form of excitement; it hurts character, demoralizes industry, breeds quarrels, tempts men to self-destruction.” But in recent years, as state legislatures have raced to legalize sports betting and gambling ads have flooded the airwaves and millions of young men have begun walking around with a casino in their pocket, spiritual leaders have been relatively muted. items.title: White House defends Trump comment to let Iran ‘take out’ LA and San Diego
items.description: Donald Trump’s remark that Iran could “take out” Los Angeles and San Diego has sparked fierce backlash from California politicians – and a strongly worded rebuttal from the White House. California Governor Gavin Newsom condemned the comment – made by Trump at a campaign rally in Nebraska – as “deranged and dangerous,” while LA Mayor Karen Bass described it as a threat and an attempt to “encourage attacks on American lives”. According to the White House, however, Trump was saying that American cities would have been threatened by Iran had he not launched a war there earlier this year. Both LA and San Diego house major US military installations including Navy ports and Air Force bases. Trump, while speaking on Monday in Nebraska about the Iran conflict, said: “It’s a small price to pay for keeping the world safe, keeping our country safe. They can take out a city. Let them take out Los Angeles, let them take out San Diego.” There were cheers from sections of the audience as the comments about the two Californian cities were made. The morning after Trump’s statement, Governor Newsom announced that the “dangerous – if not treasonous” statement had prompted him to direct California’s State Threat Assessment Center to “monitor the situation in the event that foreign actors interpret the remarks as an invitation” to target California. The agency is designed to detect and prevent security threats in the state. San Diego Mayor Todd Gloria wrote that the city was not collateral damage in a post on X, while demanding Trump keep it out of his “reckless war talk”. Trump is yet to respond to the statements made by California’s leaders. In a post on X, White House Communications Director Stephen Cheung described the “media freakout” over Trump’s comments as “not rooted in reality”. “He was clearly stating US cities would have been threatened if a nuclear Iran hadn’t been stopped,” Cheung wrote. “America is safer because of the President. Iran has no nuclear, no navy, no air force, and no money”. The president and other administration officials often claim that disrupting Iran’s nuclear programme was essential for US national security, and that any issues that have stemmed from the conflict were necessary. A separate X post from the official White House rapid response account described journalists from the Los Angeles Times reporting on the comments as “buffoons” and again pushed back against the characterisation of the comments by Newsom and others. “He was saying the US is fighting to STOP Iran from having the ability to take out LA and San Diego with a nuclear weapon — which they would if they had the chance,” the account added. San Diego, located 17 miles (27km) from the border with Mexico, is the eighth-largest city in the US and is home to Naval Base San Diego, the home port of the US Navy’s Pacific Fleet, and Naval Amphibious Base Coronado – the main training centre Navy Seals on the West Coast. It is also where Marine Corps Base Camp Pendleton is located, a base where 70,000 service members and civilians work. Located approximately 120 miles (193 KM) north of San Diego, Los Angeles is the second most populous city in the US. It is home to the space system command headquarters of the US Space Force, as well as the Los Angeles Air Force Base. Trump and Newsom met when the president visited California in January after the state was hit by wildfires This is not the first time the US president and California governor, who may run for president in 2028, have publicly clashed. Last year Trump described him as incompetent, saying he had failed to adequately respond after some of the Los Angeles anti-immigration enforcement protests turned violent. Newsom accused Trump of a “brazen abuse of power” after military personnel were deployed to secure federal buildings during those protests. Earlier this year, Trump mocked Newsom’s dyslexia, saying presidents should not have learning disabilities, which led to criticism from dyslexia charities.

items.title: 50-year-old murder suspect slumps, dies during trial in Bayelsa
items.description: A 50-year-old murder suspect, Bethlehem Nwanlia, reportedly slumped and died shortly after proceedings began at the Bayelsa State High Court in Yenagoa on Tuesday. Nwanlia was standing trial alongside two other defendants over alleged conspiracy, kidnapping and multiple murder when the incident occurred at Court 11. He reportedly collapsed in the court’s holding area shortly after Justice Amadise Michael Ekadi adjourned judgment in the case to October 27, 2026. According to people who witnessed the incident, Nwanlia suddenly clutched his chest before collapsing. Officers of the Nigerian Correctional Service, police personnel and lawyers reportedly attempted to revive him, but their efforts were unsuccessful. A medical personnel was subsequently called to examine him, after which his body was taken to a hospital for further confirmation. The Bayelsa State Judiciary’s Public Relations Officer, Mr Enoch Okunobo, confirmed the incident to newsmen on Tuesday evening. He said the deceased’s body had been deposited at the Federal Medical Centre (FMC) mortuary. “Somebody collapsed and died today. He was a murder suspect, who had been coming to court. His corpse has been deposited at the Federal Medical Centre (FMC),” Okunobo said. Nwanlia and the two other defendants were facing allegations linked to the 2022 killing of three people in Kalaba community, Yenagoa Local Government Area of the state. The allegations against the defendants had not been finally determined by the court before Nwanlia’s death. Reports also indicated that the deceased had experienced health complications while in custody. However, authorities had yet to establish the cause of his death as of the time of filing the report. The incident reportedly caused confusion among court officials, lawyers, security personnel and others present at the court premises. When contacted, the Bayelsa State Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Musa Mohammed, said he was not aware of the incident. Mohammed, however, promised to make inquiries and revert, but had yet to do so as of the time of filing the report. items.title: Asos confirms hackers sent ‘unauthorised’ notification to app users
items.description: Asos says it is investigating “unauthorised activity” involving third-party platforms it uses, after customers received a notification from its app that was sent by hackers. Dozens of people told the BBC they received the strange “ASOS HACKED” message from the clothing and beauty store’s app on Tuesday morning – with some saying it left them “scared” to open the app. The notification was addressed to the company’s data protection officer and IT teams in what cybersecurity experts said was a “brazen” extortion attempt. Asos acknowledged the “unauthorised customer notification” on Tuesday afternoon, saying some “basic personal information” may have been accessed. In an email to customers on Tuesday night, the company apologised and urged customers not to engage with the notification. It said the website and app are “operating as usual”, promising customers they can “shop with confidence” while it investigates the incident. The company has not yet informed the UK’s data watchdog, the Information Commissioner’s Office (ICO), about any breach. Exactly how many ASOS customers received the notification on Tuesday remains unclear, but Google’s Play Store says the ASOS app has been downloaded to Android devices more than 10 million times. The British retailer has a substantial global footprint – serving around 17 million customers each year across more than 150 markets. Some Asos app users in Australia, France, Sweden and the Republic of Ireland had also received the notification, according to local reports on Tuesday. Hackers seeking to put pressure on potential victims by informing their customers is rare, as most extortion happens in private, so this incident may go down as a significant moment in cyber-attack history. Shares in the company fell by around a tenth on Tuesday. Charlotte Wilson, head of enterprise at cyber-security firm Check Point, called it a “deeply serious” and “brazen” attack whereby the hackers had apparently “turned Asos’ own app into their ransom note”. But she told the BBC that Asos customers should not be “scared and frightened”, encouraging those worried to change their passwords, avoid clicking the notification link, and be cautious about possible scam emails or texts. Extortion message The message popped up on many Asos app users’ home screens on Tuesday morning Users of the Asos app appeared to have received the alarming notification at around 10:00 BST on Tuesday. Headlined “ASOS HACKED” and addressed to the company’s data protection officer and IT teams, it said: “We have fully compromised the Snowflake instance.” “Engage with us, or we will leak it,” it added, before linking to a Telegram channel. The message left many ASOS customers confused. “At first I thought it was an ad or a fun promotion like ‘ASOS HACKED get 50% off everything for a limited time only’,” Jodie, an analyst from Edinburgh, told the BBC. “Then I read the rest of the message which clearly showed that it wasn’t an ad and instead a message to IT.” Jodie’s concerns about what the Asos incident might mean for data she has shared with the platform, like her address, are shared by other users “My main concern is that my information, such as bank information, home address, telephone number, has been compromised,” said Erin, a student at the University of Sheffield. She told the BBC that while her friends have expressed similar concerns about a potential data leak, her sister did not receive the notification on the Asos app. “So the question is what is the extent? Are all customers affected even if they didn’t get the notification? It’s poor from Asos on all fronts.” Asos said in its statement that it took “immediate action to restrict access to the notification platforms” on Tuesday – adding it was working with specialists within and outside the company, as well as relevant authorities. It said it does not believe payment card information or account passwords were affected, and that its site and app are “operating as normal”. “Customer trust is incredibly important to us, and if the situation changes an update will be provided as appropriate,” it said. The BBC understands the National Cyber Security Centre has offered assistance to Asos. Meanwhile, Snowflake – whose tools are used by dozens of firms to collect, analyse and store data – told the BBC its investigation was ongoing, but it had so far found “no compromise” of its platform. The company’s services have, however, been the subject of many high-profile data breaches in recent years. Snowflake has previously been linked to cyber incidents targeting Ticketmaster and Santander. According to cybersecurity expert Jen Ellis, Snowflake collects data from multiple sources for analysis, and an “enormous” firm like Asos will have lots of data about how people shop globally. However Dan Bird, from cybersecurity firm Horizon3, said the message implied the apparent hackers’ access had gone beyond the Snowflake database. “Sending a push notification to Asos’s app users would require access to the company’s notification system, which is separate from the Snowflake data platform the attackers claim to have compromised,” he said. “If both claims hold up, it suggests the attackers got hold of credentials that opened more than one door.” What can I do to protect myself? The company has also shared a statement to the London Stock Exchange’s Regulatory News Service, which provides updates to investors. Cybersecurity experts, including Ellis, have told the BBC those behind those behind this incident are most likely trying to “apply pressure” to Asos to meet their demands, rather than target its customers. While those who received this notification will undoubtedly be concerned, it is important to know that it does not mean your phone has been hacked. We are still waiting to find out exactly what “basic personal information” may have been impacted in this incident, if any. But for now, the advice is: Do not click on links in the notification Visit Asos’s official website directly for updates Watch out for emails, texts or calls offering refunds, compensation or help with your account – scammers will exploit this type of incident when they know people are worried Try and use different passwords for your online services Enable two-step verification on email and banking accounts Keep an eye on your online transactions for anything unusual

items.title: US televangelist Jim Bakker, disgraced from sex scandal and fraud, dies at 86
items.description: US televangelist Jim Bakker, who built a multimillion-dollar media empire before being jailed for fraud and conspiracy, has died aged 86. Bakker and his then-wife, Tammy Faye, founded a Christian television programme called The PTL Club in 1974, which, at its peak, attracted 13 million viewers per day. The 86-year-old’s death was announced on Monday by his second wife Lori Bakker, who described him as “a pioneer of Christian television”. By the late 80s, Bakker and Tammy Faye’s empire began to fall apart after he became embroiled in a sex scandal and later convicted of mail and wire fraud. Tammy Faye, who divorced him in 1992, was never charged. Bakker remarried in 1998, and alongside his second wife, Lori, launched a new TV ministry in 2003. Lori Bakker described her late husband as “my best friend, and the man I was honoured to walk beside through so many seasons of life and ministry”. She did not specify the cause of death. However, Bakker’s first program The PTL Club – short for ‘Praise the Lord’ or ‘People That Love’ – was what cemented his fame with his first wife Tammy Faye. The couple built their empire with 2,000 employees and a 2,300-acre (930-hectare) Heritage USA theme park complex in Fort Mill, South Carolina. The Bakkers had a famously opulent lifestyle, owning a private jet, multiple homes, luxury cars, jewellery and even an air-conditioned dog house. In 1987, Bakker resigned from the PTL ministry after revelations of a 1980 sexual encounter with a former church secretary, Jessica Hahn. It later emerged Hanhn received a $265,000 payoff with ministry funds, resulting in Bakker being defrocked of his ministerial credentials and right to perform religious duties. Jim and Tammy Faye Bakker had a famously opulent lifestyle, owning a private jet, multiple homes and luxury cars Hahn also accused Bakker of sexual assault, though the evangelist denied this, claiming the encounter had been consensual. Bakker was then convicted in 1989 of 24 counts of mail and wire fraud and conspiracy in a scheme involving their Christian theme park, and served more than four years in prison. Tammy Faye stayed with her husband throughout the trial but divorced him in 1992 while he was in prison. She died of cancer in 2007. Following Bakker’s release from prison in 1994, he wrote a book titled I Was Wrong and married his second wife Lori in 1998. The couple began a TV ministry together in 2003 and in 2008 they began taping The Jim Bakker Show.

items.title: Assemblée nationale : Le budget de l’Etat et 16 projets de loi au menu de la 2è session
items.description: Lomé, 6 oct. (ATOP) – L’Assemblée nationale a ouvert, le mardi 6 octobre à Lomé, sa deuxième session ordinaire de l’année, consacrée principalement à l’examen et à l’adoption du budget de l’Etat. Au cours des trois prochains mois, les députés examineront également 16 projets de loi et plusieurs questions orales. La cérémonie d’ouverture a été dirigée par le président de l’Assemblée nationale, Prof. Selom Komi Klassou. Elle s’est déroulée en présence des membres du gouvernement, des présidents des institutions de la République, du corps diplomatique, des autorités locales et des gardiens des us et coutumes du Grand Lomé. L’assistance Le président de l’Assemblée nationale a dressé le bilan des activités menées pendant l’intersession. Au cours de cette période, les députés ont examiné et adopté 11 projets de loi et répondu à deux questions orales. Ils ont également pris part aux travaux de la session extraordinaire, effectué des rencontres avec leurs bases et participé à des activités de diplomatie parlementaire et de renforcement de capacités. Le professeur Selom Komi Klassou a invité les députés à accorder une attention particulière à l’examen du budget, qui constitue l’un des principaux rendez-vous de la session. Il a rappelé que le budget de l’État concerne directement la vie des populations, notamment l’éducation, la santé, les routes et pistes rurales, le développement des collectivités, l’emploi des jeunes et la sécurité. Il a fait savoir que l’examen du budget doit permettre de vérifier la cohérence entre les priorités annoncées, les moyens mobilisés et les résultats attendus. « Toute priorité appelle des moyens. Tout moyen engagé appelle une justification. Toute justification doit pouvoir être confrontée à un résultat tangible. Ces exigences fondent la rigueur de l’examen budgétaire et donnent sa portée au contrôle parlementaire. Nous aurons donc à interroger les prévisions, à apprécier les arbitrages et à examiner la capacité effective des administrations à mettre en œuvre réellement les politiques proposées. Un crédit voté ouvre une possibilité d’action. Il revient ensuite à l’exécutif de tenir la promesse et au contrôle d’en rendre compte », a-t-il indiqué. Outre le budget de l’Etat, les autres textes inscrits à l’ordre du jour porteront sur plusieurs enjeux liés à l’évolution du pays et du monde, notamment la transformation de l’économie, la protection de l’environnement, les aspirations de la jeunesse, la cohésion sociale et les mutations de l’ordre international. « Face à ces défis, la loi doit demeurer attentive aux mouvements du monde, sans jamais perdre son ancrage dans les réalités de notre pays. Cette exigence nous commande d’agir dans trois directions : Ouvrir davantage notre Parlement au monde ; donner aux députés les moyens de mieux en comprendre les bouleversements et poursuivre aussi la modernisation de l’administration parlementaire », a souligné Prof. Klassou. Les présidents des groupes parlementaires et des commissions entament leurs réunions le mercredi 7 octobre pour poursuivre les travaux de la session. Dans le cadre du renforcement de sa diplomatie parlementaire, Lomé s’apprête à accueillir, en novembre, une rencontre de haut niveau réunissant 43 parlements africains. ATOP/HKM/AO

items.title: 7e édition du « Mois du consommer local » : Le Togo mise sur les produits locaux pour renforcer sa souveraineté économique
items.description: Lomé, 6 oct. (ATOP) – La 7 e édition du « Mois du consommer local » a été lancée le mardi 6 octobre à Lomé, avec pour objectif de renforcer la place des produits et services locaux dans l’économie togolaise et de favoriser la souveraineté économique. L’édition 2026 est placée sous le thème « Consommation locale, facteur d’intégration régionale et de souveraineté économique : défis et opportunités ». Elle se déroule du 1 er au 31 octobre sur l’ensemble du territoire national. Institué par l’Union économique et monétaire ouest-africaine (UEMOA), le « Mois du consommer local » vise à encourager la consommation des biens et services produits dans les pays membres et à soutenir les différents acteurs de la chaîne de valeur, notamment les producteurs, transformateurs, distributeurs et consommateurs. La cérémonie de lancement a été marquée par la projection d’un film sur les effets de la consommation locale, des témoignages de producteurs et de transformateurs, notamment dans les filières du beurre de karité et du soja, ainsi que la remise symbolique de présentoirs destinés à mettre en valeur les produits togolais dans les supermarchés. Une visite des stands et une dégustation de mets locaux ont également agrémenté l’événement. Plusieurs activités sont prévues au cours de ce mois. Elles comprennent des expositions-ventes et des séances de dégustation à Lomé et dans les chefs-lieux de région, des ateliers de formation sur l’accès aux marchés, la qualité, le conditionnement et la fixation des prix. Une conférence-débat consacrée au thème central ainsi que des visites d’entreprises sont également programmées. 40 % du chiffre d’affaires dans des secteurs clés Le ministre de l’Economie et de la Veille stratégique, Badanam Patoki, a fait savoir que les six précédentes éditions organisées ont produit des effets positifs sur plusieurs maillons de la chaîne de valeur. Il a notamment fait état d’une progression de près de 40 % du chiffre d’affaires dans des secteurs comme l’agroalimentaire, les cosmétiques et l’habillement. Le ministre a souligné que la promotion de la consommation locale figure parmi les priorités de la Feuille de route gouvernementale 2026-2031. Il a également rappelé les mesures prises pour favoriser l’achat de biens et services locaux dans la commande publique. La digitalisation accompagne également cette dynamique. A cet effet, Patoki a salué le développement d’outils numériques locaux, notamment l’application « Nam’Asia », destinée au suivi des prix des produits de grande consommation. Le président de la Chambre de commerce et d’industrie du Togo (CCI-Togo), Dr José Kwassi Syménouh, a souligné que la consommation locale doit avant tout reposer sur la qualité, l’innovation, la disponibilité et la compétitivité des produits. « Consommer local n’est pas seulement un acte patriotique, c’est une stratégie vitale pour stimuler notre industrie, créer des emplois décents et garantir une résilience face aux défis mondiaux », a-t-il affirmé. Il a invité les producteurs à renforcer la certification et la qualité des emballages, les distributeurs à accorder davantage de place aux produits togolais et les institutions financières à adapter leurs mécanismes d’accompagnement aux besoins des transformateurs. Le représentant-résident de la Commission de l’UEMOA au Togo, Alioune Sène, a estimé que le développement des productions locales contribue à renforcer la souveraineté économique, notamment dans un contexte marqué par les crises internationales et les perturbations des chaînes d’approvisionnement. En accédant au marché des huit pays de l’UEMOA, a-t-il relevé, les produits togolais peuvent atteindre un bassin de plus de 150 millions de consommateurs, favorisant ainsi le développement de chaînes de valeur régionales. ATOP/SED/AO

items.title: Congolese-born golfer to represent Ghana at Turkish Airlines World Cup grand final
items.description: Ghana will be represented on the international golf stage this November by an inspiring golfer whose story crosses borders, cultures and communities. Louanges Kous Mang, a Congolese-born golfer from the Republic of Congo who has made Ghana her home, has earned the honour of representing Ghana at the Turkish Airlines World Golf Cup Grand Final in Antalya, Türkiye, after winning the Ghana qualifying tournament. Louanges emerged as the overall winner of the Ghana qualifier, competing alongside both male and female golfers, and secured her place at the prestigious international Grand Final scheduled to take place in Antalya in November 2026. For Louanges, the victory is about much more than a golf trophy. It represents a remarkable journey of passion, perseverance and faith, while also reflecting the power of Ghana to provide opportunities for people from diverse backgrounds to thrive. “I am incredibly grateful for this opportunity to represent Ghana,” Louanges said. “As a Congolese woman who has made Ghana my home, it is a tremendous honour to be able to carry the Ghanaian flag onto an international stage. I am proud of my Congolese roots, but I am equally proud to represent the country that has given me a home and where my golfing journey has developed.” A Global Golfing Platform The Turkish Airlines World Golf Cup is one of the world’s largest corporate amateur golf tournaments. Since its launch in 2013, the competition has grown into a truly global event, with more than 750 tournaments held across 85 countries and 130 destinations, attracting over 60,000 amateur golfers. This year alone, more than 10,000 golfers competed in over 122 qualifying events across 83 countries before the successful qualifiers earned their places at the Grand Final. The Grand Final brings together some of the best amateur golfers from around the world in Antalya, one of Türkiye’s premier golfing destinations. The 2025 Grand Final, for example, brought together 120 amateur golfers from around the world. Pakistan’s Adeel Shafqat was crowned the overall gross champion, while players from the United Arab Emirates, Algeria, Mexico, Jordan and China also claimed honours in their respective categories. The tournament has evolved beyond a sporting competition, becoming a platform that connects people and cultures through golf. Ghana on the World Stage Louanges’ qualification adds another chapter to Ghana’s growing presence in international amateur golf. Her journey also demonstrates the increasingly diverse nature of Ghana’s golfing community, where people from different nationalities and backgrounds come together through their love of the sport. For Louanges, the opportunity carries a strong personal and national significance. “I give all the glory to God for this incredible opportunity,” she said. “To stand on the international stage representing Ghana is something I do not take for granted. I will go to Türkiye with gratitude, determination and the desire to make Ghana proud.” Her qualification has also been warmly received by members of Ghana’s golfing community, who have celebrated her achievement and the opportunity it presents to showcase Ghanaian talent on the international stage. As she prepares for Antalya, Louanges will not only be carrying her golf clubs. She will be carrying the hopes and support of the Ghanaian golfing community, while proudly acknowledging the Congolese heritage that forms an important part of her story. From the fairways of Achimota to the international stage in Antalya, her journey is a reminder that sport has the unique ability to transcend borders.
