items.title: Amazon wins global rights to stream Emmys in six-year deal
items.description: Amazon Prime Video has secured exclusive global rights to stream the Emmy Awards under a six-year deal, ending the ceremony’s run on traditional US broadcast television. Starting in 2027, the agreement replaces a rotation of the gala among major networks such as ABC, CBS, Fox, and NBC. The ceremony will instead stream live for free worldwide each September, with no Prime Video subscription needed. Official terms were not disclosed. The BBC has contacted Amazon and the Emmys for comment. The move is another indication of how live events are shifting to digital platforms as viewing habits evolve. The Oscars, for example, are moving to YouTube live globally starting in 2029. Mike Proulx, research director at Forrester, said the existing setup had become out of sync with modern television. “The shows driving the industry forward largely originate on streaming platforms, yet the awards themselves were tethered to broadcast television,” Proulx said. “That’s why a leading streaming service like Prime Video makes sense for the Emmys’ next act.” Cris Abrego, chair of the Television Academy, said the deal gives the ceremony “unprecedented global reach”, allowing audiences in more than 200 countries to watch live. “Television has never been more global, and the Emmys should be a celebration that the world can share,” Abrego said in a statement issued by Amazon. Mike Hopkins, head of Prime Video and Amazon MGM Studios, said the platform is honoured to serve as the “global home” for the ceremony, adding that streaming the show for free delivers ” the best entertainment to our customers worldwide.” The agreement marks a milestone for Amazon, giving Prime Video its first marquee entertainment broadcast after building a live-sports profile centred on the NFL’s Thursday Night Football, NBA, and UEFA Champions League fixtures. Amazon’s latest earnings highlighted strong gains in live viewership , including record ratings for its inaugural NBA season, which peaked at 6.5 million viewers for Game 7 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals. The Emmys deal positions Amazon directly alongside Google, whose video platform YouTube holds the upcoming Oscar rights. YouTube relies primarily on an ad-supported model, whereas Amazon is leveraging free live access to draw massive global audiences into its wider ecosystem. Like its live sporting events, the free broadcast will allow Amazon to build a substantial global advertising footprint. Moving exclusively to Prime Video is significant for the Emmys, ending a rotation across the major legacy broadcast networks that has been in place since 1955 and marking the first time the gala will leave traditional broadcast television entirely. First held in 1949, the Emmys honor achievements in acting, writing, and production, serving as a primary showcase for the global television industry.

items.title: European Film Festival returns to Ghana after a 5-year break
items.description: The European Film Festival has returned to Ghana after a five-year break, with this year’s edition focusing on peace, tolerance and inclusion. The festival was launched in Accra by the Minister for Tourism, Culture and Creative Arts, Abla Dzifa Gomashie, who says Ghana has no shortage of creative talent but needs more platforms to help young creatives develop their skills and gain exposure. She believes opportunities that allow emerging filmmakers to interact with other players in the industry can help them build their expertise and take their work further. “We’re not a short supply of creatives. We’re a short supply of the platforms that’s available to them. And I think that is why when we have these opportunities, we should seize them because it helps you to build your expertise, to see how other people are doing what they are doing and also to meet Ghanaian film producers.” The Minister also urged young creatives to take advantage of opportunities created through the festival and other platforms available to them. According to her, Ghana has the opportunity to correct distorted narratives by telling its own stories and presenting a stronger image of the country to international audiences. EU Ambassador to Ghana, Rune Skinnebach, said the festival is about more than screening films. He said it is also intended to create opportunities for artists to connect with their European counterparts and gain platforms to take their stories to wider audiences. “But the festival is more than movies. The festival is about creating a platform for artists, Guinean artists, to be exposed to European artists, but also to get them a platform from which they can continue to tell their amazing stories to the wider audience. So this is why we have these movies tonight and this is why we have the European Film Festival also.” The festival features film screenings and creative engagements aimed at bringing filmmakers, artists and audiences together. The 2026 edition is expected to provide opportunities for creative exchanges between Ghanaian and European industry players.

items.title: À Rabat, le RNI prépare une offensive judiciaire contre des élus locaux ayant quitté ses rangs
items.description: Le Rassemblement national des indépendants (RNI) n’entend pas tourner rapidement la page des dernières élections législatives à Rabat. Ébranlé par la perte de deux sièges parlementaires dans les circonscriptions de l’Océan et de Chellah, le parti dirigé par Aziz Akhannouch prépare une contre-offensive politique et juridique visant certains élus et responsables locaux ayant quitté ses rangs tout en conservant des fonctions acquises sous son étiquette. Selon des sources informées, le parti de la Colombe s’apprête à activer les mécanismes prévus par la loi organique n°113.14 relative aux communes afin de saisir la justice administrative contre plusieurs responsables locaux. Cette démarche intervient dans un contexte marqué par des tensions internes et des mouvements de transhumance politique observés lors de la séquence électorale récente. Au cœur de cette stratégie figure notamment le cas de Fatiha El Moudni, maire de Rabat. Élue avec le soutien du RNI, celle-ci a rejoint il y a quelques semaines le Parti authenticité et modernité (PAM), tout en demeurant à la tête du conseil communal de la capitale. Le parti estime disposer d’un fondement juridique pour engager une telle procédure. L’article 51 de la loi organique relative aux communes prévoit en effet qu’un membre élu d’un conseil communal peut être déchu de son mandat lorsqu’il abandonne, au cours de son mandat, le parti sous les couleurs duquel il a été élu. Le même texte autorise le président du conseil concerné ou le parti politique ayant présenté le candidat à saisir le tribunal administratif, lequel est tenu de statuer dans les délais prévus par la loi. D’après les mêmes sources, le RNI considère que plusieurs « dépassements et comportements inacceptables » ont été enregistrés parallèlement aux dernières élections législatives. Ces agissements justifieraient, selon elles, le recours aux dispositions de la loi organique pour rétablir le respect des règles partisanes. Des sources de Hespress évoquent ainsi des « comportements de déloyauté et de trahison » observés lors du scrutin, particulièrement à Rabat. Elles soulignent que certains responsables ont annoncé leur retrait de l’action politique menée au nom du parti tout en conservant les postes obtenus grâce à son investiture. Pour ces interlocuteurs, « ces comportements nécessitent un recours à la justice administrative afin de rétablir l’ordre organisationnel et juridique ». La direction du parti serait par ailleurs confrontée à une pression croissante de la part de candidats et de militants qui s’estiment victimes de « trahisons électorales » dans plusieurs circonscriptions de Rabat, Salé et Témara, notamment celles de l’Océan et de Chellah. Selon ces sources, l’absence de réaction risquerait d’affecter durablement la crédibilité du parti et d’affaiblir la confiance de ses bases militantes dans les décisions prises par ses instances dirigeantes. Au-delà du contentieux juridique, ces développements ravivent également les interrogations sur la gestion interne des investitures lors des dernières élections. Les mêmes sources attribuent une partie des difficultés rencontrées par le RNI à la désignation de candidats « imposés », ne disposant ni d’un ancrage local solide ni d’une base électorale suffisamment établie. Une situation qui aurait conduit à la perte de sièges que le parti considérait comme acquis ou, à tout le moins, stratégiques. Selon cette lecture, l’imposition de certains profils aurait fragilisé le dispositif électoral du parti et facilité la progression de formations concurrentes. Le RNI aurait ainsi perdu des sièges remportés lors des élections de 2021, un recul que plusieurs responsables jugent aujourd’hui difficilement justifiable. À l’approche des prochaines élections communales, la direction du parti semble décidée à tirer les conséquences de cet épisode. Les sources consultées indiquent qu’un réexamen de plusieurs dossiers locaux est envisagé et que des actions judiciaires pourraient être engagées contre les élus ayant rompu leur lien partisan tout en conservant des responsabilités au sein d’institutions élues. The post À Rabat, le RNI prépare une offensive judiciaire contre des élus locaux ayant quitté ses rangs appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: PTA backs teachers’ strike, threatens street protest if gov’t misses October 30 deadline
items.description: The National Council of Parents Teachers Association (PTA) has backed the concerns of striking pre-tertiary teachers, warning that parents will join the unions in street protests if the government fails to meet its October 30 deadline for resolving outstanding issues. Secretary of the Council, Raphael Kofi Gapson, said parents recognise the legitimacy of the teachers’ grievances and believe government must honour its commitments. Speaking on JoyFM’s Top Story , he said parents initially supported the strike because they shared the teachers’ concerns and wanted government to take concrete steps to resolve the dispute. “We saw that as a genuine concern,” he said. Mr Gapson, however, urged teachers to consider returning to the classroom while negotiations continue, saying parents are hopeful the ongoing discussions will lead to a resolution by the end of the week. “We only hope and pray that since the Finance Minister is part of these discussions and they’ve firmed up concrete measures, we cannot say that we would want to throw away the baby with the bathwater. There should be a way around it,” he said. He said parents would give government until October 30 to demonstrate concrete progress in fulfilling its commitments to teachers. Mr Gapson warned that failure to meet the deadline would compel the PTA to join the teacher unions in protest. “We are telling government too that if by the 30th we don’t see any concrete steps, we’ll be on the street with the teacher unions to demonstrate against government,” he stated. He stressed that teachers have legitimate financial obligations that must be honoured, arguing that the issue is one of national priorities. Mr Gapson also expressed optimism that the negotiations between government and the teacher unions could resolve the impasse and allow schools to return to normal operations. His comments follow renewed negotiations between the teacher unions, the Fair Wages and Salaries Commission (FWSC) and the Ghana Education Service (GES), which ended without an agreement on Tuesday. The parties are expected to reconvene on Wednesday, October 7, as efforts continue to resolve the issues that triggered the nationwide strike.

items.title: Paramount takes over Warner Bros in $110bn Hollywood merger
items.description: Paramount Skydance has officially taken over Warner Bros. Discovery in a $110bn merger that is set to reshape Hollywood and the media landscape. The takeover – merging two of the biggest studios in Los Angeles – comes after months of legal disputes and widespread criticism over feared cuts and consolidation could harm competition and consumers. It will alter streaming for millions, usher in a new chapter in the film and TV industry, and leave one of the biggest US news outlets, CNN, in uncertain territory. The merger will also bring together a host of entities including HBO, CBS, Nickelodeon, Showtime, Comedy Central, DC Studios and Food Network. Paramount will acquire ownership of iconic franchises that include Harry Potter, Game of Thrones, The Lord of the Rings to add to its existing catalogue of hit franchises which includes Indiana Jones, Mission: Impossible and Shrek. The newly merged entertainment behemoth will be re-branded under the name Skydance Corporation, the company originally founded by David Ellison before he took over both Paramount and Warner Bros Discover. Ellison, chairman and chief executive of Skydance, said the completion of the deal was “historic” for the film industry. “From the start, our ambition was to bring these two storied studios together and create a stronger competitor, with the talent, resources, and reach to tell great stories in every genre, on every platform, for audiences everywhere. Now that ambition is a reality,” he said. Asked about the merger after it had been finalised, US President Donald Trump described the deal as “great”. “They’re terrific people and it’s going to be a great company,” he said. Last week, Ellison named the outgoing chief executive of Mattel, Ynon Kreiz, as co-chief executive. Kreiz will focus on the company’s day-to-day operations, including integrating the newly-combined businesses, while Ellison will focus on strategy and technology. Mark Thompson – who once served as director general of the BBC – will continue in his role as chairman and editor-in-chief of CNN Worldwide, while Bari Weiss remains editor-in-chief of CBS News. Casey Bloys, who has lead HBO and Max Content, will be the co-chair and chief content officer for direct-to-consumer content. Mike Proulx, research director at Forrester Research, said that change “essentially means the HBO leadership team is now in charge of Skydance’s combined streaming operation”. “While that bodes well for the HBO brand, make no mistake, Bloys will be pressured to find and deliver cost efficiencies that could affect content quality,” he warned. Dan Coatsworth, head of markets at AJ Bell, said the company has high debts at a time when interest rates are high. “The combined entity, now called Skydance, needs to cut costs and make bigger profits to be able to get the debt down to more manageable levels,” he said. “The fact Tom Cruise movie Digger, Warner Bros’ last release before the merger, has been a major flop is a reminder of how the film industry is not a guaranteed ticket to riches.” Rocky path to merger While the company said it had received unanimous approval from competition authorities across the world, the long running takeover process has featured controversy since the beginning. Netflix initially had a deal to buy part of Warner Bros Discovery, but Paramount Skydance launched a bidding war, leading to the streaming giant walking away. Lawyers in about a dozen US states then filed lawsuits – led by California – aiming to block the deal, arguing it would stifle competition, raise consumer prices and cause “substantial” harm to movie theatres, cable distributors and “ultimately, audiences nationwide”. US states announced a settlement with Paramount and Ellison last month which paved the way for the merger to go ahead . As part of the deal, Paramount has agreed to establish a “news editorial independence board” to “ensure independent, objective, fact-based reporting” at CNN and CBS. Politics and editorial independence has become an area of concern at CBS since the news broadcaster was taken over in 2025 as part of separate a merger between Skydance Media and Paramount. Ellison, who hosted a dinner for President Donald Trump earlier this year, has sought to reassure people that editorial independence will be maintained. Over its 103-year-old history, Warner Bros has won more than 100 Academy Awards – including dominating at last year’s show with a record-tying 11 Oscars for One Battle After Another, Sinners and Weapons. Paramount traces its roots back 1912 and also boasts more than 100 Oscars for classics spanning from The Godfather to Titanic, though the studio has not mirrored the same recent spate of Hollywood honours. The studio was not nominated for any projects last year by the Academy. Its last win came in 2022 with Top Gun: Maverick. The deal with US states aims to ensure the merged studios will produce “real, robust movies” that will generate economic activity and put people back to work, said California Attorney General Rob Bonta, who led the lawsuit and settlement. To prevent the studio from fulfilling its annual quota with low-budget or automated content, the deal includes strict guardrails against “AI-generated” films. As part of the agreement, Paramount must release at least 30 films each year. If it fails to meet its annual production quota, it will be forced to sell its 49% stake in Miramax, the film company founded by disgraced Hollywood mogul Harvey Weinstein and his brother Bob. Paramount also must ensure 20% of all film production takes place in the US for the first two years, rising to more than 30% through the following three years.

items.title: Suspend offshore gold exploration licence – NAFAG urges gov’t
items.description: The National Fisheries Association of Ghana (NAFAG) has appealed to the government to suspend an offshore reconnaissance licence granted to Gold Coast GRC Ghana Ltd. for gold exploration along Ghana’s shallow continental shelf, pending further consultations with the fishing industry. In a petition dated October 6, 2026, signed by the association’s President, Nana Joojo Solomon, and addressed to the President, NAFAG demanded clarification of the potential implications of the exploration programme for fisheries resources, marine habitats and coastal livelihoods. The association, which represents five major fisheries groups, said its concerns centered on the size of the licensed area, stakeholder consultation, and the application of fisheries and environmental safeguards. NAFAG said the company held 10 offshore reconnaissance licences covering about 10,000 square kilometres along approximately 300 kilometres of coastline between Half Assini and Winneba, extending about 33 kilometres offshore. It said the company’s published map appeared to indicate that parts of the licensed area could fall within the Inshore Exclusion Zone (IEZ), which extends up to 12 nautical miles, or about 22 kilometres, from the coastline. The association said the precise extent of any overlap should be established through the publication of the official cadastral coordinates and licence instruments. NAFAG also raised concerns about the proximity of the licensed area to Greater Cape Three Points, where Ghana launched its first Marine Protected Area at Busua on April 14, 2026, as part of efforts to strengthen marine conservation. Assessment NAFAG’s concerns also relate to Section 50 of the Fisheries and Aquaculture Act, 2025 (Act 1146). The provision requires a person planning an activity, other than fishing, that is likely to have a substantial impact on fishery or other aquatic resources to inform the Fisheries Commission before the activity begins. The Commission may subsequently require a Fisheries Impact Assessment or make recommendations to prevent or minimise potential adverse impacts. NAFAG said it had not established whether the applicable fisheries assessment process had been completed in relation to the project and called for clarification from the relevant authorities. NAFAG also questioned the consultation process, saying that although a stakeholder meeting was held at the Accra City Hotel on July 9, 2026, it had not received the report of the meeting. NAFAG therefore called on the government to establish the precise location and conditions of the licences, clarify the applicable fisheries and environmental safeguards, and ensure meaningful consultation with affected stakeholders before the programme advances. It urged President Mahama and the relevant agencies to suspend further exploration pending those steps, arguing that Ghana’s marine resources must be managed in a manner that protects fisheries, food security and coastal livelihoods while allowing responsible investment in the country’s natural resources.

items.title: Libya’s parliament speaker ousted after 12 years
items.description: Libya’s parliament speaker, a supporter of eastern strongman Khalifa Haftar, was ousted on Tuesday after 12 years in the post, in what experts said may be a sign of a shifting political balance. MPs voted to replace Agila Saleh with Al-Salhin Abdelnabi al-Obeidi, the parliament’s spokesman announced on X. Libya has been beset by violence and instability since the overthrow of Muammar Gaddafi in 2011. It remains divided between the UN-recognised government in Tripoli led by Prime Minister Abdulhamid Dbeibah, and a rival administration in the east backed by military commander Haftar. Haftar’s camp relies in particular on the parliament, which sits in the eastern city of Benghazi under their control. Saleh, 82, has long been considered a staunch ally of the Haftar clan, but he appeared to be weakened as Haftar’s sons, in particular Saddam Haftar, consolidated their positions. Emadeddin Badi, an analyst at the London-based Chatham House, said: “Agila Saleh appears to be the latest casualty of Saddam Haftar’s drive to centralize decision-making in eastern Libya and bulldoze his way into a political role.” His removal comes as a US initiative aimed at reviving the political process and unifying Libya’s institutions is under discussion. The post Libya’s parliament speaker ousted after 12 years appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: El Malick Ndiaye en Guinée : « Ce que nos concitoyens attendent, c’est que la loi trouve son chemin vers l’école, le centre de santé, le marché et l’emploi »
items.description: Le Parlement de la République de Guinée a tenu, ce lundi 5 octobre 2026, la rentrée solennelle de sa 10e législature, placée sous le thème : « Construire la Guinée de 2040 : la 10e législature au cœur de la souveraineté, de la prospérité et de l’intégrité africaine ». Dans la salle des congrès du Palais du Peuple de Conakry, la capitale guinéenne, plusieurs représentants de parlements africains, notamment ceux de la CEDEAO, du Sénégal, du Mali, de la Côte d’Ivoire, de la Sierra Leone, du Gabon, du Togo et du Libéria, ainsi que des Conseils nationaux de transition (CNT) de la Guinée-Bissau et du Mali, se sont succédé au pupitre pour prononcer leurs discours. Au nom du président de l’Assemblée nationale du Sénégal, El Malick Ndiaye s’est adressé directement aux représentants des peuples africains présents dans la salle en ces termes : « Monsieur le Président, honorables députés, je voudrais revenir à ce qui constitue, au fond, la raison d’être d’une législature : produire des lois, certes, mais surtout faire en sorte que ces lois produisent des effets dans la vie des citoyens. Le jour de votre élection, Monsieur le Président, vous avez tenu une phrase que je me permets de reprendre parce qu’elle dit l’essentiel : « Les lois pour les lois, non. » Cette exigence, nous la connaissons. Un Parlement a parfois la faculté trop aisée de produire du texte. Le Journal officiel, c’est ainsi. Mais la vie des gens à Conakry, comme à Dakar, ne suit pas nécessairement », a-t-il déclaré dans un passage de son discours. Selon le vice-président du Parlement sénégalais, « Ce que nos concitoyens attendent, c’est que la loi votée dans cette salle trouve son chemin vers l’école, vers le centre de santé, vers le quartier, vers le marché, vers l’emploi. L’effectivité n’est pas une formule. C’est la distance qui sépare le texte de la personne à qui il est destiné. Et chez nous, à Dakar, cette distance reste encore trop longue ». Cet élu sénégalais, qui a eu le privilège de siéger au gouvernement avant d’accéder au perchoir, a indiqué que la perception du Parlement diffère selon que l’on se trouve du côté du gouvernement ou de celui des députés. « Le ministre juge parfois que la question vient de l’autre. Le député découvre parfois que la réponse porte sur un autre sujet que celui qui a été posé. Ces deux impressions peuvent être sincères. Mais aucune des deux ne suffit à faire une démocratie. Ce qu’il faut, c’est le retour de la question, six mois plus tard, avec les chiffres, avec les résultats, avec le nom du quartier rien a changé. C’est ici que se situe l’un des enjeux majeurs de notre Parlement: passer progressivement du contrôle politique au contrôle de la performance ». Par ailleurs, le vice-président du Parlement sénégalais, El Malick Ndiaye, a plaidé pour une coopération parlementaire plus concrète et axée sur les résultats. « Il faut des commissions qui tiennent au sujet. Des rapports que l’on reprend au lieu de les classer. Des ministres que l’on réentend, non pour les mettre en difficulté, mais pour vérifier si la réponse donnée en mars dernier tient en octobre. Sur ce point, le Sénégal n’apporte pas une leçon. Il apporte un chantier, le même que le vôtre. Et sans doute le même que celui de beaucoup de parlements. C’est précisément là que notre coopération parlementaire peut devenir concrète : comparer nos méthodes, partager nos expériences et rapprocher davantage la décision publique de ses effets réels ». Mamadou Yaya Barry L’article El Malick Ndiaye en Guinée : « Ce que nos concitoyens attendent, c’est que la loi trouve son chemin vers l’école, le centre de santé, le marché et l’emploi » est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: ‘LOCK THE CLOCK!’
items.description: P resident Trump is in a race against time. There are 28 days until the midterms. There are 837 days left in his presidency. There are actuary tables noting the challenges of battling Father Time for 80-year-old men. But, at the moment, he is focused on one particular slice of time: daylight savings. It has become the latest obsession for a man known for not letting go of his compulsions. He has tilted against windmills, told the government to stop procuring paper straws, and spent significant mental and rhetorical energy openly discussing which is worse: electrocution in a sinking electric boat or being devoured by a shark. His attention has been pulled to daylight savings by pending legislation that would end the requirement to change clocks twice a year to match the seasons, moving an hour back in the fall and then jumping forward in the spring. Instead, he wants to keep the clock where it is after springing forward—ensuring more sunlight in the evening—and not falling back, which allows for more light in the mornings during winter months. “LOCK THE CLOCK!” the president wrote on social media over the weekend. Trump has offered a number of anecdotal arguments to support his view. During an interview with the conservative commentator Wayne Allyn Root in August, he claimed that he was once an hour late for an important meeting—“a big person from a big country”—because he had forgotten to reset his clock. He then claimed that stopping the time change would deter crime, “because criminals sleep late, you know; they do their crime in the evening.” He has suggested that it’s unsafe and costly for workers to have to reset clocks on church steeples or government buildings twice a year. He has also said that getting rid of daylight savings would lower people’s risk for cardiac issues and stroke, limit seasonal depression, and boost tourism. [ Read: A different kind of fading president ] But perhaps Trump’s most fundamental motivation became evident late last month: A president who likes to golf would like more sunlight to do so. During the final day of the Presidents Cup, held at a Chicago-area country club on September 27, Trump met with the PGA Tour Chief Executive Brian Rolapp and discussed daylight savings. A few days later, Rolapp sent Trump a letter urging him to ensure that there is more sunlight in the evenings. Too many golfers are busy with their lives and struggling to get in enough time on the course, he argued—a problem made even worse when the clocks fall back. “An extra hour of evening light sounds simple, but for everyday Americans, it can be the difference between getting on the course and not,” Rolapp wrote. The change, he said, would generate 23 million additional rounds of golf each year and pump $1 billion into the golf industry. All of this seemed to register with Trump, who operates multiple golf clubs, and who made the letter public two days later. In a midterm election in which many voters are angry about prices at the pump or in the grocery-store aisles, a closing message from the president is to stand up for the rights of golfers to get an extra hour on the green. T his particular president has known few constraints during his return to the White House. Without congressional approval, he has gone to war with Iran, torn down the East Wing, renamed large bodies of water, and closed the Kennedy Center . But Trump has not attempted to halt the changing of the clocks himself, instead conceding that he needs Congress to pass the Sunshine Protection Act. The House has passed the bill, but Trump has met resistance in the Republican-controlled Senate. “It’s dead as disco,” Senator John Kennedy of Louisiana, a Republican, told Reuters last week. Trump has fixated on one particular Republican holdout: Senator Tom Cotton of Arkansas. Last weekend, the president took the unusual step of posting what he claimed was the Republican’s cellphone number and urging Americans, particularly those in Arkansas, to call Cotton and demand that he vote for the bill. Cotton’s office did not respond to my requests for comment, but he has said on social media that although “no one likes changing the clock,” not doing so would mean “absurdly late sunrises” during winter months. In Fayetteville, Arkansas, the sun would rise close to 8:30 a.m. “Arkansans don’t want their kids going to school in the pitch dark,” he wrote. When I tried the number that Trump posted, I was greeted by a cheery automated message: “Sorry, the mailbox is full, and there is not enough space to leave a message. Goodbye!” H istorians have traced the idea behind daylight savings back to Benjamin Franklin. In 1784, he wrote a satirical letter to the editor arguing that the government should make sure that sleep patterns coincide with the sun as a way to save money on candles. It would take more than a century for the idea to become reality: Congress enacted daylight saving time in 1918 to help conserve energy during World War I. Although Woodrow Wilson tried to keep the change permanent, Congress overrode his vetoes, and the experiment with shifting the clocks ended. But at the urging of President Franklin Roosevelt, it was reinstated in 1942 during World War II, with a new slogan: “War Time.” When the war ended, Congress again dropped the practice. In the decades afterward, some states adopted different standards, creating a confusing patchwork of time zones. William Markowitz, a time scientist at the United States Naval Observatory, at one point concluded that “the United States is the worst timekeeper in the world.” Iowa alone had 23 methods for starting and ending daylight saving time. For a brief period in Minnesota, St. Paul moved clocks forward for daylight savings while neighboring Minneapolis did not. Police officers in St. Paul wore two watches. Congress stepped in to create a national standard with the Uniform Time Act in 1966. Clocks would spring forward in April and fall back in October. In 1973, Congress ended the practice once again after President Richard Nixon called for the change in an address to the nation. But public support crumbled during the winter months because kids were going to school in the dark. The New York Times called it the “Second Dark Age,” and the experiment ended after less than a year. Since then, there has been some tinkering—shifting what month the clock changes, for example—but not wholesale changes. [ Read: The war over daylight saving time ] Trump’s own stance has evolved. In March 2019, he posted on Twitter in support of making daylight savings permanent. Five years later, he reversed himself: “Daylight Saving Time is inconvenient, and very costly to our Nation.” Last March, three days before clocks were scheduled to spring forward, Trump was again indecisive. Americans seemed evenly divided on the issue, he told reporters in the Oval Office, making it “hard to get excited about it.” He said he could see the argument from both sides. Some people want more light later in the day, he said, whereas others like having the light early in the morning. But a few weeks later, perhaps tired after losing that hour, he was clear that he wanted daylight at the end of the day. “Very popular and, most importantly, no more changing of the clocks.” In May, as the legislation marched toward House approval, Trump was again animated, and said the country had to end “this ridiculous, twice yearly production.” He added: “It will also be a very nice WIN for the Republican Party. Take it!” It doesn’t appear that the Republican Party is going to follow his advice.

items.title: Investigators meet family, community over deaths of 3 children found in car trunk
items.description: Investigators probing the deaths of three children found in the boot of a vehicle belonging to a Ghana Immigration Service officer have met with family and community members in Tamale as efforts intensify to establish what led to their deaths. The engagement, which took place on Tuesday evening, brought together investigators, the Northern Regional Police Command and the Regional Command of the Ghana Immigration Service. According to JoyNews sources, investigators took statements from some community members as they worked to piece together the events surrounding the deaths of Dauda Abdul Aziz, 3, Saani Alsharaf, 5, and Dauda Fadilan, 7. The bodies of the three children were discovered in the boot of a black Hyundai Tucson at Koblimahagu Zoo in the Tamale Metropolis on Monday, October 5. The children had reportedly left home on Sunday morning to attend Islamic classes but failed to return. Their bodies were later found inside the vehicle, which police said was stuck in mud. The biological parents of the deceased have also been invited to the Regional Police Command to assist with the investigation as authorities seek further information about the circumstances surrounding the deaths. The development comes after preliminary autopsy findings indicated that the children did not die of natural causes, prompting police to treat the case as a murder investigation. A toxicological examination is expected to provide further information on the cause and circumstances of their deaths. The Inspector-General of Police has deployed a specialised team comprising homicide investigators, crime scene experts and intelligence officers to support the Northern Regional Police Command. The vehicle has also been secured for forensic examination as investigators work to determine how the children ended up in the boot and what caused their deaths. Investigations are ongoing, with authorities expected to provide further updates as more evidence emerges.

items.title: Ondo Crash: ADC questions NAF aircraft maintenance funding
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress, ADC, has questioned the implementation of defence budgets for the maintenance of Nigerian Air Force aircraft following Monday’s crash of an ATR-42 aircraft at Igbokoda, Ondo State. The opposition party said the tragedy should not only prompt investigations into the immediate cause of the crash but also renewed scrutiny of how much money meant to keep military aircraft operational is actually released and spent. In a statement released in Abuja on Tuesday by its National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, the ADC described the crash as tragic and unfortunate and expressed condolences to the families of the victims. The party said official figures showed that as of December 2025, only N4.5 billion, representing about 13.98 per cent of the N34.71 billion budgeted for the maintenance of Nigerian Air Force aircraft, had been released. By contrast, it said N20.74 billion was allocated for the maintenance of the Presidential Air Fleet, with N20.27 billion, representing 97.76 per cent, released within the same period. “Put simply, while the fleet that serves a handful of people in power got almost every kobo it asked for, the fleet that serves and protects 200 million Nigerians was left with crumbs,” the ADC said. The party stressed that it did not want to prejudice the ongoing investigation into the crash but said the incident provided another opportunity to examine the funding and maintenance of military equipment. “While we do not intend to prejudice ongoing investigations into the cause of this tragic crash, we believe that this sad moment also provides an opportunity to raise, yet again, questions about the non-implementation of the defence budget and the perennial neglect of military equipment,” it said. The ADC said the safety of military personnel should receive the same level of attention as the safety of political leaders. “The safety of the President matters. But what also matters is the safety of the pilots and airmen who put their lives on the line in defence of the country. Patriotism does not replace spare parts, and condolence messages do not take the place of accountability,” the party maintained. The party therefore called for the crash investigation to go beyond determining the immediate cause of the accident to examining the maintenance of defence equipment, particularly the Nigerian Air Force fleet. It also demanded an audit of maintenance expenditure and budgetary releases to determine whether funds appropriated for the upkeep of military aircraft were released and properly utilised. The post Ondo Crash: ADC questions NAF aircraft maintenance funding appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Algérie et l'effet Boomrang
items.description: Il y a Octobre rose. Celui des rubans délicats, des campagnes de sensibilisation et des élans de bienveillance universelle pour tous les seins. Il y eut Octobre rouge. Celui de la Révolution, des défilés militaires sur la place Rouge, des commissaires politiques et de la Pravda — ce merveilleux journal où la vérité avait au moins la décence de ne jamais changer de ligne éditoriale. Et puis, il y a Octobre Conseil de sécurité. Pas besoin de ruban rose. Pas besoin de faucille ni de marteau. Pas même besoin de rallonge téléphonique. Il suffit désormais d’un vieux Minitel diplomatique : 36 15 CONSEIL Tapez 1 pour la MINURSO. Tapez 2 pour l’autodétermination. Tapez 3 pour l’autonomie. Tapez 4 pour connaître la réaction d’Alger. La connexion est en cours. Ne raccrochez pas. L’Histoire est en ligne. Et surtout, ne touchez pas au clavier : le logiciel est peut-être ancien, mais il fonctionne encore. Le logiciel 1975 Nous voici donc en octobre 2026. Le Conseil de sécurité revient sur le dossier du Sahara occidental, à quelques semaines de l’expiration du mandat de la MINURSO, fixé au 31 octobre. Des consultations sont annoncées les 7 et 8 octobre, avant le vote attendu sur la prolongation de la mission. Autrefois, on attendait le tiercé du dimanche. Aujourd’hui, on attend New York. Avec une différence essentielle : si le cheval arrive mauvais dernier, on perd seulement son pari. Si la diplomatie vous impose une mise à jour du logiciel, c’est toute une stratégie nationale qu’il faut réinstaller. Et voilà précisément le problème. Pour comprendre la situation actuelle, il faut remonter aux années 1970. C’était une époque merveilleuse. Le monde était divisé en deux blocs, les colonels portaient très bien l’uniforme, les révolutionnaires avaient toujours raison et les monarchies étaient priées de comprendre qu’elles appartenaient à une époque révolue. Dans cette grande kermesse idéologique, le Maroc souffrait d’un vice rédhibitoire : il avait un Roi. Pour une partie de la gauche révolutionnaire européenne, c’était presque une maladie politique. Une monarchie ? Aïe. Une monarchie arabe ? Double aïe. Une monarchie arabe avec une profondeur africaine, une histoire millénaire et des alliances occidentales ? Appelez immédiatement le service après-vente de la Révolution. Dans ce décor, le dossier du Sahara allait devenir un formidable instrument de géopolitique régionale. Le mouvement sahraoui fut progressivement intégré dans une lecture idéologique où tout semblait simple : colonisation → décolonisation → référendum → indépendance. C’était propre. C’était binaire. C’était pédagogique. Et surtout, cela permettait de ne jamais poser la question la plus inconfortable : que faire lorsque le réel refuse de suivre le scénario ? L’étrange besoin d'un ennemi Mais derrière le dossier saharien se trouve peut-être une question plus profonde : que devient un système politique lorsque sa cohésion dépend durablement de l’existence d’un ennemi ? L’histoire de l’Algérie indépendante fournit, à cet égard, une succession de scènes où la confrontation ne semble jamais très éloignée du centre du pouvoir. La guerre de libération avait opposé le mouvement national au pouvoir colonial. Puis vint l’indépendance, et presque immédiatement, les rivalités internes prirent le relais : la lutte armée, les frontières, les rivalités entre responsables révolutionnaires, Ben Bella contre Boumediene, puis Boumediene contre BenBella, les redressements révolutionnaires, les purges, les règlements de comptes, les recompositions successives du pouvoir. L’ennemi pouvait changer de visage, mais il fallait qu’il existe. Hier colonial, puis contre-révolutionnaire, comploteur, traître, opposant, et enfin ennemi extérieur. Et lorsque l’ennemi extérieur devient politiquement utile, il possède une qualité extraordinaire : il permet de remettre à demain les questions que l’on ne souhaite pas poser aujourd’hui. Pourquoi réformer ? Le contexte régional est dangereux. Pourquoi ouvrir le débat ? L’ennemi nous observe. Pourquoi changer de logiciel ? La souveraineté est menacée. Pendant ce temps, le logiciel continue de tourner. On pourrait presque parler d’une gouvernance par l’alerte permanente. La question devient alors presque naïve : combien de responsables civils et militaires ont été arrêtés, écartés, condamnés ou emprisonnés au cours de l’histoire politique algérienne ? Combien de Premiers ministres ? Combien de généraux ? Combien d’anciens compagnons de route devenus, à un moment ou à un autre, des adversaires du système ? Plus le poste est élevé, plus le chemin vers la prison est court. Le chiffre importe finalement moins que le mécanisme. Lorsqu’un système politique transforme régulièrement ses propres anciens serviteurs en adversaires, il produit une étrange géométrie du pouvoir : l’ennemi n’est jamais très loin. Il peut même avoir travaillé hier à vos côtés. Le paradoxe devient alors saisissant. Pour préserver l’unité nationale, il faut un adversaire. Et lorsque l’adversaire devient moins commode à l’intérieur, l’histoire offre toujours une solution de secours : regarder à l’extérieur. Le voisin devient alors plus qu’un voisin : un miroir, un repoussoir, un élément de politique intérieure. Le problème commence lorsque l’existence de l’adversaire devient une condition de fonctionnement du récit politique. Car à force de chercher l’ennemi partout, on finit par avoir besoin qu’il existe. Et c’est peut-être ici que commence le véritable effet boomerang. Le caillou dans la babouche Le pari semblait pourtant séduisant : un conflit territorial suffisamment long pour épuiser l’adversaire, une cause suffisamment noble pour mobiliser les chancelleries, une rhétorique suffisamment ancienne pour donner l’impression qu’elle était éternelle, et un voisin suffisamment proche pour que le problème reste toujours à portée de main. Le caillou était lancé. On pensait qu’il resterait dans la chaussure marocaine. Erreur de calcul. Car le problème avec les cailloux que l’on glisse dans la chaussure des autres, c’est qu’après quelques décennies, on finit parfois par marcher soi-même dessus. Pendant des années, la diplomatie algérienne a récité la même formule avec la régularité d’un vieux téléscripteur : décolonisation → autodétermination → référendum. Le monde, lui, a changé de système d’exploitation. L’URSS a disparu. La guerre froide est devenue un chapitre de manuel. Kadhafi est entré dans l’Histoire. Les révolutionnaires en treillis et en échec scolaire sont devenus des gestionnaires d’État. Les idéologies ont perdu leur éclat. Le pétrole a cessé d’être une réponse universelle. Et pourtant, quelque part dans le disque dur de la diplomatie maghrébine, le fichier Sahara_1975_FINAL_VRAIMENT_FINAL continuait de tourner. Erreur 404 : logiciel 404 incompatible avec le réel C’est là que commence la partie la plus intéressante. Le Conseil de sécurité a adopté, le 31 octobre 2025, la résolution 2797. Elle a prolongé le mandat de la MINURSO jusqu’au 31 octobre 2026. Le texte réaffirme la recherche d’une solution politique juste, durable et mutuellement acceptable, fondée sur le compromis et compatible avec le principe d’autodétermination. Il prend également acte du soutien de plusieurs États à la proposition marocaine d’autonomie et affirme qu’une véritable autonomie sous souveraineté marocaine pourrait constituer une solution particulièrement réalisable. Autrement dit, le dictionnaire diplomatique n’a pas supprimé le mot autodétermination. Il lui a simplement ajouté quelques voisins encombrants : réalisme, compromis, pragmatisme, autonomie, négociation. Quand un vieux logiciel rencontre une nouvelle version du monde, il ne dit jamais : « Nous nous sommes trompés de siècle. » Il préfère afficher : « Nous procédons à une réévaluation séquentielle des paramètres du processus. » Le Minitel, lui, aurait été plus franc : Erreur 404 : logiciel 404 incompatible avec le réel. Le plus grand tour de magie: dispraitre du vote Il y eut même, le 31 octobre 2025, un petit moment de théâtre diplomatique particulièrement savoureux. Le Conseil de sécurité adopta la résolution 2797 par 11 voix pour, aucune contre et 3 abstentions. L’Algérie, elle, ne participa pas au vote. Il faut reconnaître à la diplomatie algérienne un véritable talent scénique. Quand on n’aime pas le résultat, il existe plusieurs solutions : voter contre, s'abstenir, protester. Ou, solution plus élégante: ne pas participer. C’est un peu comme quitter le stade avant la fin du match et expliquer ensuite que l’on conteste le score. La diplomatie moderne invente décidément des formes très raffinées de présence par absence. Mais le plus embarrassant n’est peut-être même pas le vocabulaire de la résolution. C’est le décor qui change. Le texte adopté par le Conseil de sécurité accueille l’initiative de Staffan de Mistura visant à faire avancer les discussions et mentionne explicitement la disponibilité des États-Unis à accueillir des négociations. Ainsi donc, après des décennies de théâtre diplomatique, le dossier revient à la table des négociations. Et cette fois, le scénario ne se joue plus seulement à New York : Madrid, Washington, New York. Le Sahara a découvert le tourisme diplomatique. Il ne manque plus qu’un guide Michelin : « Trois capitales, quatre délégations, une proposition d’autonomie et beaucoup de café diplomatique. » Le paradoxe du caillou er le petit poucet Pendant ce temps, le Maroc a fait ce que font souvent les pays lorsqu’ils se sentent durablement contestés : il a cherché à transformer l’obstacle en stratégie. Le caillou destiné à faire trébucher le Petit Poucet l’a finalement obligé à regarder plus loin : Plus loin vers l’Afrique, Plus loin vers l’Atlantique, Plus loin vers les infrastructures et les ports, Plus loin vers les alliances internationales et les provinces du Sud, Plus loin encore vers une diplomatie redéfinissant une profondeur stratégique. C’est là que l’histoire devient franchement ironique : le caillou devait empêcher le Maroc d’avancer ; il lui a fourni une direction. Il était une fois un Petit Poucet maghrébin. Un voisin avait décidé de lui semer des cailloux sur le chemin pour le faire trébucher, l’épuiser, l’isoler et l'enfermer dans un conflit interminable. Mais le conteur géopolitique avait oublié une règle élémentaire des contes : les cailloux servent parfois à retrouver son chemin. Le Petit Poucet les ramassa, les transforma en repères, puis construisit une route, un port, une stratégie et des alliances. Et pendant que l’Ogre comptait les cailloux depuis sa clairière, le Petit Poucet avait déjà changé de paysage. L'ogre a-t-il raté son coup? L’Ogre n’est plus exactement celui des contes du XXe siècle. Il ne porte plus nécessairement l’uniforme ni le grand livre de la révolution. Il parle désormais le langage de la rente, de la mémoire, de la souveraineté et de la fidélité aux vieux récits. Le problème apparaît lorsqu’une mémoire devient une politique étrangère qui ne sait plus comment sortir de son propre récit. Car il arrive un moment où l’Histoire cesse de demander : « Qui avait raison en 1975 ? » et commence à demander : « Qui sait encore quoi faire en 2026 ? » Le véritable boomrang Voilà le véritable effet boomerang : vous lancez un projectile idéologique dans les années 1970. Vous le regardez voler pendant quarante ou cinquante ans. Vous changez de président, de système économique, d’alliés, de génération et de vocabulaire, mais vous oubliez de changer de trajectoire. Et un beau matin d’octobre 2026, le projectile revient. Il revient après avoir fait le tour du monde diplomatique, estampillé de tampons de Washington, d’escales à Madrid et de consultations à New York, avec une résolution du Conseil de sécurité en poche et une inscription sur la carrosserie : « Mise à jour disponible. » On clique sur installer, et soudain : « Votre logiciel historique n’est plus compatible avec cette version du réel». 36 15 SAHARA Octobre rose s’achèvera avec ses rubans. Octobre rouge appartient aux musées et aux historiens. Mais Octobre Conseil de sécurité nous rappelle une vérité beaucoup moins romantique : les conflits peuvent durer longtemps, mais les logiciels géopolitiques finissent toujours par devenir obsolètes. La MINURSO attend sa nouvelle feuille de route. Le Conseil de sécurité attend les négociations. Les diplomates attendent les diplomates. Et Alger attend peut-être encore que le monde revienne à 1975. Il risque d’attendre longtemps. Le Minitel est mort, la Pravda a changé d’époque, Kadhafi n’est plus là pour distribuer les cailloux, et les vieux blocs ont disparu. Mais le serveur de l’Histoire, lui, fonctionne toujours : 36 15 SAHARA Résolution en cours de téléchargement. Veuillez patienter. La réalité est enfin en ligne. *Université Cadi Ayyad – Safi – The post Algérie et l'effet Boomrang appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.description: Emission d’une série de quatre timbres-poste sur le thème « École pour tous : Inclure les élèves ayant des besoins spéciaux à l'école et lutter contre le harcèlement » La Poste Tunisienne a émis lundi 5 octobre 2026, une série de quatre timbres-poste sur le thème « École pour tous : Inclure les élèves ayant des besoins spéciaux à l'école et lutter contre le harcèlement ». Ces timbres-poste ont été conçus dans le cadre de la manifestation « Philakids », organisée en partenariat avec le ministère de l’Éducation et le ministère de la Famille, de la Femme, de l’Enfance et des Personnes âgées. Cette initiative visent à sensibiliser à l’importance d’un environnement scolaire inclusif et sûr, fondé sur l’acceptation de la différence et l’égalité des chances, à favoriser le vivre-ensemble au sein de l’école et à bannir toute forme de harcèlement et de discrimination. Ces timbres-poste ainsi que les autres produits philatéliques réalisés à cette occasion sont disponibles à la vente, depuis hier, dans tous les bureaux de poste et via Internet à travers le site dédié . Communiqué L’article Philakids | La Poste émet 4 timbres dédiés à l'égalité des chances à l'école est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Disparition de Boualem Boualem : l’hommage émouvant de la Présidence
items.description: Boualem Boualem , chef de cabinet de la Présidence de la République, s’est éteint lundi 5 octobre dans un hôpital de Genève en Suisse. Sa dépouille a été rapatriée ce mardi et le président Abdelmadjid Tebboune, dont il était très proche, lui a rendu un dernier hommage à l’aéroport d’Alger. Peu après, la Présidence de la République a salué un « homme de droit au service de l'État et de la Nation ». « Le défunt Boualem Boualem nous quitte ; avec sa disparition, nous saluons un patriote authentique et un haut cadre de l'État. À tous les postes de responsabilité et dans toutes les missions qu'il a assumées, il était un exemple d'engagement, gardien de la confiance placée en lui, fidèle à sa patrie et à son travail», a écrit la présidence de la République dans un hommage émouvant à ce grand commis de l’État. La Présidence de la République que Boualem Boualem a rejoint dès 2020, soit quelques semaines seulement après l’élection du président Tebboune en décembre 2019, souligne ce qui a fait la force de ce magistrat discret qui occupait le poste de chef de cabinet à El Mouradia depuis novembre 2023. Boualem Boualem : disparition d’un homme qui « jouissait » de la confiance de Tebboune Il tirait « l’estime » et la « considération » dont il jouissait de la « richesse de son parcours de magistrat et de sa connaissance avisée du domaine juridique et judiciaire, ainsi que son expérience et sa sagesse dans la gestion », a souligné la présidence. Boualem Boualem bénéficiait de la « confiance du Président de la République, Abdelmadjid Tebboune, occupant successivement les fonctions de conseiller aux affaires juridiques et judiciaires, puis de directeur de cabinet de la Présidence de la République ; des fonctions dans lesquelles il a fait preuve d'un « dévouement absolu », accomplissant ses missions avec une « rigueur » et une « précision exemplaires », poursuit la présidence. « Avec sa disparition, nous perdons un responsable compétent, un patriote dévoué et un homme de haute stature et de grande noblesse ; un être cher qui a rendu l'âme à son Créateur », conclut la Présidence dans son hommage. L’article Disparition de Boualem Boualem : l’hommage émouvant de la Présidence est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Teacher strike: FWSC blames new allowance demand for deadlock with teacher unions
items.description: The Chief Executive Officer of the Fair Wages and Salaries Commission (FWSC), Dr George Smith-Graham, says that negotiations between the commission and the striking pre-tertiary teacher unions have stalled over a demand for the introduction of a new allowance. According to Dr Smith-Graham, the FWSC is currently operating under a transitional arrangement as Ghana moves towards the establishment of the Independent Public Emoluments Commission (IPEC). He explained that under this arrangement, unions whose conditions of service have expired are expected to focus on improving existing allowances rather than undertaking comprehensive negotiations on new conditions of service. Speaking on Accra-based Channel One TV on Tuesday, October 6, Dr Smith-Graham said the teacher unions’ demand for a new allowance had become a major point of disagreement in the negotiations. “The transitional arrangement is that the Fair Wages and Salaries Commission is in transition, and so within this transitional arrangement there should be no holistic negotiations on conditions of service.” “They are supposed to be identifying allowances within the unions whose conditions of service have expired and enhance them, but they are looking at it differently. They want even an introduction of a new allowance, and that is what we are discussing.” The impasse comes as the Ghana National Association of Teachers (GNAT), National Association of Graduate Teachers (NAGRAT) and Pre-Tertiary Education Teachers Association of Ghana (PRETAG) continue their nationwide strike over outstanding concerns relating to their conditions of service, promotion arrears and allowances. A meeting between the FWSC, the Ghana Education Service and the three unions on Tuesday ended without an agreement, with the parties expected to reconvene on Wednesday. The unions have indicated that the strike will remain in force until their concerns are resolved. Dr Smith-Graham, however, said the FWSC remained committed to engaging the unions despite the disagreement over the scope of the negotiations. “It’s a mandate the rank and file has given to them so we have no choice but to engage them and let them know that this is the situation,” he said. He also dismissed suggestions that the FWSC entered the negotiations without the necessary authorisation from the Finance Minister. “Absolutely not,” he said, insisting that he had been given a mandate by the Finance Minister since January. According to Dr Smith-Graham, the FWSC has negotiated with 59 unions and organisations this year, with several of those engagements being concluded within a few hours. He attributed the difficulty with the teacher unions to what he described as their attempt to move beyond the transitional arrangement currently guiding the negotiations. “It is a struggle because maybe, to put it bluntly, they are trying to go out from the transitional arrangement that we have. That is what is bringing about the change,” he said. Despite the disagreements, the FWSC CEO said negotiations would continue as the Commission seeks to reach an agreement with the unions. “I want to finish this negotiation before the end of the week,” he said.

items.title: National Cathedral: ‘There’s no clarity as to what they want to use the site for’ – Afenyo-Markin on site’s future
items.description: Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin has urged the government to take a clear decision on the future of the National Cathedral project, arguing that the facility could serve purposes beyond Christian worship. According to him, the National Cathedral has the potential to become a major tourist attraction and a national landmark if completed. Mr Afenyo-Markin made the call during a meeting between the Minority Caucus and the Christian Council of Ghana on Tuesday, October 6, 2026. He said the project should not be viewed solely as a place of worship, but also as a facility capable of attracting tourists and contributing to Ghana’s image. “This national cathedral – we need it as a nation. It shouldn’t be too simplistic that a cathedral is just for prayer. It is also for tourism. I went for a training program in Turkey recently, and at an old mosque, people troop there just to go and take pictures. “They said 4,000 visitors a day. So if we have the cathedral, it’s not only for the Christian community; it is for the entire nation. A tourism potential, its image and the image of the country; it becomes a rallying point for us as a country.” His comments come as the government reviews the future of the stalled National Cathedral project. The project site has recently been handed back to the government, while the Attorney-General reviews a forensic audit into expenditure on the project. Mr Afenyo-Markin criticised what he described as a lack of clarity and consistency from the government on its intentions for the project. “The government is showing inconsistency. It says one thing today, it says another tomorrow. We don’t know what they want to use the site for. There’s no clarity as to what they want to use the site for. But I believe that this is one matter that we must all sit together and look at. “So it’s a matter that I want you to take us on board, and we’d love to discuss further.” The Minority Leader therefore called on the Christian Council to engage with the issue as discussions continue over the future of the project.

items.title: Investigators meet family, community over deaths of 3 children found in car trunk
items.description: Investigators probing the deaths of three children found in the trunk of a vehicle belonging to an immigration officer have met with family and community members Tuesday evening to seek information about the incident. The meeting brought together the Northern Regional Police Commander and the Regional Commander of the Ghana Immigration Service, underscoring the gravity of a case that has drawn national attention. According to JoyNews sources, investigators took statements from some community members as part of efforts to piece together the circumstances that led to the deaths of Dauda Abdul Aziz, 3, Saani Alsharaf, 5, and Dauda Fadilan, 7. The childrens’ bodies were discovered in the boot of a black Hyundai Tucson at Koblimahagu Zoo in Tamale. The biological parents of the deceased have also been invited to the Regional Police Command for further probing as the investigation intensifies. The engagement comes as police have reclassified the case as murder after an autopsy revealed the children did not die of natural causes. The Inspector-General of Police has deployed homicide investigators, forensic and crime scene experts, and intelligence officers to support the Northern Regional Command. Investigations are still ongoing.

items.title: Teachers have legitimate concerns, but prolonged strike will affect pupils – Joseph Kumah
items.description: Vice Chairman of Parliament’s Education Committee, Joseph Kumah, has acknowledged the concerns raised by pre-tertiary teacher unions but appealed to them to consider the impact of their continued strike on pupils. Speaking on Joy FM’s top story, Mr Kumah said teachers have a legitimate basis for demanding that government honour its commitments, particularly regarding outstanding payments and conditions of service. “Our teachers, they are right to some extent, because anybody that is promised something definitely, they should receive that promise.” However, he cautioned that prolonging the industrial action could have consequences for teaching and learning, particularly for pupils who rely on public schools. “… we should know that the more we are absent from the classrooms, the more it is going to affect children.” Mr Kumah said Parliament’s Education Committee has been concerned about the dispute and has been engaging stakeholders as part of efforts to find a resolution. He said the committee supports efforts to ensure that government fulfils its commitments to teachers but also wants the dispute resolved in a way that allows teachers to return to the classroom. His comments come amid renewed negotiations between government and the teacher unions over outstanding promotion arrears, allowances and the renewal of their collective bargaining agreement. The nationwide strike by pre-tertiary teachers remains in force as the parties continue discussions aimed at resolving the dispute.

items.title: Ahafo NHIA Beats 2025 Target to Secure Second Year of Universal Health Coverage
items.description: The Ahafo Region has attained Universal Health Coverage (UHC) in access within the National Health Insurance Authority’s (NHIA) operational scope, recording 87 per cent population coverage in 2025, representing 110 per cent of its target. The achievement marks the second consecutive year that the region has attained UHC within the NHIA’s operational scope. The Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of the NHIA, Dr. Victor Asare Bampoe, speaking at the inauguration of the Asunafo South district office at Kukuom on Wednesday, September 30, 2026, commended the Ahafo Region for its sustained UHC performance. Dr. Bampoe stressed that the achievement was a milestone rather than the end of the journey. He urged the Regional and District teams to sustain the progress by registering every eligible resident, strengthening active membership, and ensuring that people in remote communities could confidently access healthcare when they needed it. The CEO also commended Ahafo for being the first region to implement the One-Time Attendance Code (OTAC) system, which he said was strengthening accountability, reducing identity fraud, and protecting public funds. Dr. Bampoe said the progress represents more than a physical structure, describing it as a commitment to better access, improved service delivery, and a closer connection between the NHIA and the people of Asunafo South. “Our responsibility is significant,” he said, adding that at the heart of health insurance was not a card, computer, digital code, or building, but the people who depended on the NHIS to access healthcare. He therefore charged staff of the Authority in the region to continuously serve with professionalism, integrity, patience, compassion, and urgency, reminding them that the quality of service must match the quality of the milestone achievement. Ahafo Regional Director, George Mawuli, said the region is proud of its UHC achievement, saying that it comes with a task—sustaining the momentum through registering every eligible resident and strengthening active membership. He expressed gratitude to Dr Asare Bampoe and his team for their continuous support to the activities of the NHIA in the Ahafo region. Mr. Mawuli indicated that sustaining health requires the support of the Authority in our operational needs, including infrastructure, logistics, staffing, internet connectivity and other resources needed to sustain the gains. This milestone directly advances the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) 3 (Good Health and Well-Being) by accelerating target 3.8 on Universal Health Coverage and financial protection. It further aligns with SDG 1 (No Poverty) by safeguarding vulnerable rural families from out-of-pocket health costs, SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure) through tech-driven reforms like OTAC, and SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities) by extending care to remote communities. Public health and policy experts point out that while achieving 87 per cent enrollment successfully breaks down financial barriers to entry, the focus must now shift to maintaining service readiness across remote facilities. Health economists also highlight that pioneering digital tools like OTAC serve as a vital safeguard against identity fraud and billing leakages, ensuring long-term financial sustainability for national health schemes across sub-Saharan Africa.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo opens door for Portugal return, apologises for walk-out
items.description: Cristiano Ronaldo has confirmed his continued availability for Portugal after explaining his decision to leave the national team camp and accusing head coach Jorge Jesus of breaking an agreement over his playing time. The 41-year-old Al Nassr forward had raised questions about his international future following his departure from the squad, but said he remained committed to representing Portugal. “If I am physically well, playing for my club, with goals I hope, after serving the suspension that may be applied to me, I will be available, as I have always been until today, to compete and win for our national team,” Ronaldo said in a statement shared with Reuters. Ronaldo also apologised to his teammates and the Portuguese public for leaving the camp, adding that he would accept any disciplinary action imposed by the Portuguese Football Federation. The forward left the squad after remaining an unused substitute during Portugal’s 2-1 away victory over Norway in the Nations League on September 27. According to Ronaldo, he and Jesus had previously agreed that he would miss the Norway and Denmark matches as part of a plan to manage his fitness. However, Ronaldo said the coach changed the arrangement on the day of the Norway match and told him he would play for 30 minutes. “Everyone knows the rest. I warmed up from halftime onwards, watched the minutes tick by and wasn’t called on,” he said. “The manager had broken his word to me.” Ronaldo said it was the second time he believed Jesus had failed to honour an understanding between them and that the coach’s public comments did not correspond with their private discussion. “It was the second time he had broken his word to me. I decided to leave the training camp without waiting for any further broken promises,” he said. Jesus, however, denied after Portugal’s victory over Norway that he had reached such an agreement with Ronaldo, while leaving the door open for the veteran forward to return to the national team. Ronaldo also rejected suggestions that he had interfered with tactical or technical decisions during his international career. “Never, at any moment, have I interfered in any technical or tactical decision of any coach or national team manager in almost 25 years of career,” he said. “I accept, for better or worse, what they propose that I do. I respect the decision, and when they break their word to me, I feel that my place is not there.” Addressing speculation about a possible farewell to international football, Ronaldo said he expected to have one or more farewell matches in the future but remained focused on competing for Portugal. “I can promise all my fans, naturally and especially all Portuguese people, that we will have one or more farewell matches; there will be time for that. But when I think of the national team, what I really think of is competing,” he said. Ronaldo, Portugal’s record goalscorer and most-capped player, has scored 146 goals in 234 international appearances. He also recalled remaining with the Portugal squad following the death of his father during an international camp, saying his commitment to the national team had remained strong throughout his career. The dispute between Ronaldo and Jesus has cast uncertainty over the forward’s immediate international involvement, but his latest statement makes clear that he intends to remain available for Portugal, subject to his fitness and any disciplinary sanction. items.title: 22 ans pour … un accident (Le billet de Omar DIOUF)
items.description: Déjà 1.068 accidents et 41 morts au premier semestre 2026 à Louga. Ces données livrées par l’Agence nationale de la sécurité routière (Anaser), le mardi 29 septembre dernier, dans la capitale du Ndiambour, n’ont presque pas ému beaucoup de concitoyens dans le pays. Au même moment, un compatriote, chauffeur de camion aux États-Unis, était jugé pour avoir provoqué un accident ayant entraîné la mort de trois membres d’une famille. Le sieur Ngom risque une peine de 22 ans de prison, au verdict du 29 octobre prochain. De quoi alerter l’opinion sénégalaise sur ce dur réquisitoire. Toutes les vies se valent, mais l’on doit se demander pourquoi la mort des trois citoyens américains dans « un seul » accident est plus « cher payé » que les « 41 morts » des 1.068 accidents dans la région de Louga en 2026 ? La sévérité de la peine requise aux Usa est sans doute dissuasive pour amener tout conducteur de véhicule à se montrer prudent au volant et plus attentif sur la route. Et la sanction sénégalaise de « un mois » est bien différente des « 22 ans » de celle américaine… omar.diouf@lesoleil.sn
