items.title: PTI long march: CM Afridi-led convoy camps in Mattani for the night, heads to Khyber next
items.description: PESHAWAR: The PTI convoy led by Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Tuesday reached Mattani, located on the outskirts of Peshawar — its latest stopover in the party’s long march that is being carried out to demand the release of jailed party founder and ex-prime minister Imran Khan. PTI Information Deputy Secretary in KP Ikram Khatana told Dawn that the protesters, who set out from Kohat earlier in the day, would spend the night in Mattani. “They will leave for Khyber at 2pm tomorrow,” he said. The march began on Sunday (Oct 4) from Lakki Marwat, and the Afridi-led convoy reached Kohat on Monday night. The protesters aim to reach Khairabad — which borders Punjab — by Oct 8, where the KP chief minister will announce the next plan of action. And while the plan for the trek beyond Khairabad is yet to be announced, the PTI — which is in the government in KP and in the opposition in the Centre — had previously announced Islamabad as its final destination. However, the Centre has warned the party against any protest or gatherings in Islamabad. But, PTI decided to embark on the march after weekend talks with the federal government to bridge their differences failed for multiple reasons , particularly over the counterterrorism policy. Before setting out for Mattani, CM Afridi addressed the PTI supporters at University Chowk in Kohat and criticised the federal government over its counterterrorism policy. “Your failed policy did not end terrorism. Let me propose a policy under which peace can be established in 100 days,” he said, according to a statement released by his office. He said he was “not afraid of anyone and neither are the youth of KP”. “I have shared the draft of my demands on social media”, he continued, referring to a set of proposal he said he had sent to the opposition team negotiating with the government last week. CM Afridi said if any of his demands was unconstitutional or illegal, he would cancel the long march. The provincial chief executive rued that the PTI had employed all legal and constitutional means for the fulfillment of its demands, including meetings with Imran. But when one was not served justice, the Constitution allowed for peaceful protest, he added. He said the PTI would protest peacefully. He maintained that the people wanted a resolution of their issues through the provincial government’s policy, adding that there had been military operations in KP for the past 22 years but terrorism was still prevalent. “Your failed policy did not end terrorism. Let me propose a policy under which peace can be established in 100 days,” he remarked. He added that once they would decide to move to Islamabad, nobody would be able to stop them. Referring to the PTI postponing the launch of its march from Sept 27 to Oct 4, he said “they now have problem that this is Test match”. CM Afridi also said that there were reports that Imran’s health was again deteriorating in jail. He said if “Imran’s health is played with or he suffers any harm”, the jail administration, prime minister and other relevant authorities would be responsible. March will not be allowed to move beyond Attock: Kundi Earlier in the day, KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi vowed that PTI’s long march would not be allowed to proceed beyond Attock in Punjab — which borders KP — saying the party “did not have the capacity” to do so. Kundi made the remarks while speaking to Geo News programme ‘Geo Pakistan’. “They cannot go any further than Attock,” Kundi said, challenging PTI to “try to take a step”. He contended that the party did not have “enough capacity” to march further. “They claim to have two million people with them […] show us the people; they don’t have the capacity.” Kundi said the province was suffering from terrorism and “yet, they [PTI] want to march to Islamabad instead”. Speaking about his recent meeting with Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi in Peshawar, the governor recalled that the two often held meetings to discuss the security situation, and during last week’s meeting, the two also discussed “dialogue with the PTI as well as the way forward in relation to PTI’s long march”. Kundi cautioned: “If there is a mishap during the long march — especially if someone from southern KP who wants to reach Islamabad to carry out a plot [is involved] — what screening mechanisms does PTI have in place to prevent that from happening?” He also assailed the PTI-led KP government for “staying silent” on terrorist incidents. “When the federal government asks for their support against militancy, they say that the army should leave the province and that we should hold a dialogue with Afghanistan,” Kundi said, accusing the incarcerated PTI founder of “having militants settled in KP in the past”. “He was called Taliban Khan,” Kundi added, referring to Imran. Kundi further claimed that KP Chief Minister Afridi was taking “directions from PTI leader Murad Saeed”, whom the governor described as a “runaway”. He vowed that Saeed “will be brought before the people and made to pay for his actions”. Speaking about the possibility of governor’s rule in KP, Kundi said: “If the president and prime minister hand the task to the province […] and deem governor’s rule necessary, the province will ensure its implementation.” He held that governor’s rule was the last resort. “Surgery is the last option; first, you are put on medication. No one wishes to do it,” he said, referring to governor’s rule. “We want to continue, but if you are pushed to the limit and there is no option left, then it is considered.” On Monday night, after reaching Kohat’s Lachi tehsil, CM Afridi said while addressing PTI supporters that this time, the party’s struggle was a long one that required endurance and sustained mobilisation, according to a statement issued by his office. “We must not exhaust ourselves. Our struggle is a long one,” he said, adding that, however, from Oct 8 onwards, a “T20 match” would begin. Kundi also posted on social media that he had chaired an “important security meeting” with KP Chief Secretary Shahab Ali Shah, KP’s Inspector General of Police (IGP) Zulfiqar Hameed, and other senior officials. “The province cannot afford complacency when terrorism, crime and law-and-order challenges continue to threaten our people,” Kundi said, calling on the provincial government to “make the safety of its people its foremost responsibility”. “Political activity cannot come at the expense of security, and every institution must focus on protecting lives and maintaining peace,” he added. Separately, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also urged the PTI to end its long march and invited the opposition to sit with the government to resolve contentious issues through political dialogue. The march so far After launching the already-postponed march from Lakki Marwat on Sunday afternoon, the KP CM’s caravan reached Karak at night, where Afridi addressed supporters at Jail Chowk. Ahead of the march, movement on several roads in KP’s Dera Ismail Khan, Upper and Lower South Waziristan, Tank and Hangu was restricted under Section 144 for varying periods . On Sunday, former KP CM Ali Amin Gandapur, who was leading PTI workers from DI Khan to Lakki Marwat, took a U-turn from Yarik because of road blockades and the prevailing law and order situation. Noting that Section 144 had been imposed in the area for three days, Gandapur stressed that the party leadership had clearly directed workers not to damage public property or engage in any activity that could worsen the situation. Nevertheless, he contended that the return should not be viewed as a withdrawal from the protest movement, but as a temporary decision. In Karachi , a planned protest campaign in different areas was disrupted after police deployed personnel at several locations, blocked roads and detained several party workers and leaders. The PTI claimed that police detained more than 75 of its leaders and workers, including women, from different parts of Karachi. It further alleged that arrests made in other parts of Sindh, including Sukkur, put the total number of detained PTI workers across the province at more than 100. On Saturday night, an opposition delegation comprising PTI and Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-i-Ayin-i-Pakistan (TTAP), and a joint team of the government and PPP held hours-long negotiations , which ended in a deadlock.

items.title: Innovative Teachers threatens legal action over exclusion from Collective Bargaining Agreement negotiations
items.description: A dispute has emerged between the Innovative Teachers Union and the Ghana National Association of Teachers (GNAT) over the former’s exclusion from negotiations for the 2026 Collective Bargaining Agreement covering teaching staff of the Ghana Education Service. Innovative Teachers, through its lawyers, has issued a demand notice to the Attorney General and other stakeholders, threatening legal action if it is not allowed to participate in the ongoing negotiations. In a letter dated October 5, 2026, the union argued that although GNAT holds the collective bargaining certificate, it is required under the Labour Regulations, 2007 (L.I. 1833), to consult or, where appropriate, invite other unions representing the same class of workers to participate in negotiations. The union accused GNAT of failing to consult it during the 2020, 2024 and 2026 collective bargaining processes. Innovative Teachers further alleged that GNAT consulted the National Association of Graduate Teachers (NAGRAT) and the Pre-Tertiary Teachers Association of Ghana (PRETAG) ahead of the 2026 negotiations but did not extend the same opportunity to it. It therefore wants the Fair Wages and Salaries Commission (FWSC) to require GNAT to provide evidence that Innovative Teachers was consulted before the 2026 negotiations continue. The union is also demanding either its inclusion in the negotiations or the withdrawal of NAGRAT and PRETAG from the negotiating table, leaving GNAT to negotiate alone with the FWSC. It warned that failure to resolve the matter could result in an application to the court to suspend the implementation of the 2026 Collective Bargaining Agreement. However, GNAT has rejected the claim that Innovative Teachers has a legal right to participate in its negotiating committee. In its response to the National Labour Commission, GNAT argued that being a registered trade union and wanting to participate in negotiations does not automatically confer a legal right to do so. According to GNAT, it is the holder of the collective bargaining certificate for teaching staff of the Ghana Education Service, while Innovative Teachers does not hold such a certificate. It relied on provisions of the Labour Act, 2003 (Act 651), particularly Sections 99, 101 and 103, to argue that negotiating authority is vested in the trade union that holds the collective bargaining certificate. GNAT also distinguished between consultation and participation under Regulation 10(1) of L.I. 1833. It acknowledged that the regulation imposes a duty on the certificate holder to consult other unions representing the same class of workers but argued that the decision to invite another union to participate in negotiations is discretionary. GNAT said the regulation uses the phrase “where appropriate” in relation to participation, unlike the mandatory language used for consultation. It maintained that it had considered whether Innovative Teachers should be invited to the negotiations and determined that such participation was not appropriate. The association also rejected the argument that its previous inclusion of other unions, including NAGRAT, created a continuing legal obligation to include all other unions in subsequent negotiations. It described such previous participation as an exercise of discretion rather than an admission of a legal requirement. GNAT further argued that compelling it to include every union representing teachers could make collective bargaining unworkable, given the possibility of multiple unions representing the same class of workers. It said the collective bargaining certificate system was designed to ensure that one recognised union negotiates on behalf of the entire class of workers. The association also disputed the characterization of its position as an unfair labour practice, arguing that GNAT is a trade union and not an employer. According to GNAT, the conditions of employment of teachers are determined through negotiations involving the Ghana Education Service and the Fair Wages and Salaries Commission, and its decision on the composition of its negotiating committee is an internal governance matter. It therefore urged the National Labour Commission to reject Innovative Teachers’ request to compel its inclusion in the negotiations. Innovative Teachers, however, maintains that GNAT’s exercise of its discretion must comply with the constitutional requirement to act fairly and without discrimination. It has consequently called on the relevant authorities to intervene before the 2026 Collective Bargaining Agreement negotiations proceed further.

items.title: 17-member committee formed to address concerns over Adipa landfill
items.description: A 17-member committee has been formed to help address concerns raised by residents of Adipa and surrounding communities over waste disposal activities at the Adipa Engineered Landfill Site. The committee was constituted after a stakeholder meeting involving traditional authorities, local government officials, community representatives, the Member of Parliament for Nsawam-Adoagyiri, Frank Annoh-Dompreh, and officials of Waste Landfills Company Limited and Zoomlion Ghana Limited. The meeting, convened on Tuesday, October 6, by the Aburihene and Adontenhene of the Akuapem Traditional Council, Otubour Gyan Kwasi, followed concerns over the transportation of waste from parts of Accra to the Adipa landfill. Residents had raised environmental and public health concerns and called for greater consultation over activities at the facility. The committee will be chaired by the Chief of Nsawam, Nana Kofi Sarh, following authorisation by the Aburihene. Zoomlion Chief Executive Officer, Dr Joseph Siaw Agyepong, is also a member. Dr Agyepong acknowledged the concerns raised by the affected communities and announced a package of interventions intended to support Adipa and neighbouring communities. These include the construction of a health centre and a water project, community-wide fumigation exercises and periodic health screening for residents. He also pledged scholarship support for beneficiaries from the eight affected communities to pursue studies in Russia, while indicating that additional assistance could be considered based on community needs. Mr Annoh-Dompreh welcomed the engagement and commended Dr Agyepong for meeting directly with residents to hear their concerns. The Minority Chief Whip, who had previously called for greater stakeholder engagement over the transportation and disposal of waste at Adipa, stressed the need for traditional authorities, local assemblies, community leaders and residents to be consulted before major waste-management activities are undertaken. The Municipal Chief Executive for Nsawam-Adoagyiri, Philibert Selorm Fummey, also welcomed the interventions and appealed for the establishment of a waste treatment facility in the municipality. He said such a facility could help add value to waste received at the site and create jobs rather than relying solely on waste disposal. Mr Fummey said concerns surrounding the Adipa landfill had been among the issues he discussed with Dr Agyepong after assuming office. The Municipal Chief Executive for Akuapem South, Paul Osae Offei, said the return of stakeholders to the negotiating table demonstrated their willingness to work together to address residents’ concerns. He called for stronger collaboration between Akuapem South and Nsawam-Adoagyiri to ensure communities in both municipalities benefit from the agreed interventions. The Aburihene urged residents to cooperate with Waste Landfills Company Limited and Zoomlion to facilitate implementation of the commitments. The newly constituted 17-member committee is expected to monitor the implementation of the interventions, follow up on outstanding concerns and provide a platform for continued engagement between the affected communities, traditional authorities, local government and the waste-management companies.

items.title: L’Algérie s’impose difficilement contre le Niger, la défense inquiète
items.description: L’équipe d’Algérie ne rassure pas. Face au Niger ce mardi au stade Hocine Ait Ahmed de Tizi-Ouzou, elle n’a pas brillé. Cueillis à froid par les visiteurs grâce à un but de Jocelyn (13 e ) qui s’est facilement joué de la défense algérienne pour tirer et marquer, les hommes de Brahim Hemdani ont longtemps attendu avant de revenir au score grâce à un coup franc sublime de Bachir Belloumi (1-1, 54 e ). L’attaquant de Hull City a commencé le match sur le banc, avant de prendre la place d’Ibrahim Maza avant la pause (41 e ). Un exploit personnel du fils de la légende du football algérien qui illustre l’incapacité des Fennecs à concrétiser leur domination avec 65% de possession de balle. Après ce but, Brahim Hemdani a opéré plusieurs changements en faisant entrer Adil Boulbina, Ramy Bensebaini, Amin Chiakha, Adil Bourabaa, Achref Abada et Fares Chaibi. Ces permutations n’ont pas changé la physionomie du match, avec des Verts inefficaces. Algérie – Niger : les Fennecs confirment leur fébrilité en défense Il a fallu attendre la 73 e minute pour voir Adil Boulbina s’infiltrer dans la surface nigérienne, avant d’être dangereusement fauché par un défenseur adverse. Le penalty obtenu a permis à Ramy Bensebaini de donner un avantage définitif à l’équipe d’Algérie. Le Niger a failli égaliser dans les derniers instants de la rencontre avec notamment un tir repoussé par le poteau algérien. Cette courte victoire obtenue après le succès face à la Zambie (3-1) vendredi 25 septembre et le nul contre le Burundi (2-2) le 29 septembre confirme les difficultés des Fennecs en défense et le travail gigantesque qu’attend le sélectionneur Brahim Hemdani pour remettre l’équipe nationale sur les rails. L’article L’Algérie s’impose difficilement contre le Niger, la défense inquiète est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: « IA » une crise de la gouvernance mondiale (Par Seydou KA)
items.description: «L’efficacité de l’action technique est-elle forcément source de progrès moral ? ». Ce sujet proposé à l’épreuve de philosophie lors du baccalauréat sénégalais 2025 renvoie à une phrase souvent citée de Condorcet et datant de 1787 selon laquelle « plus la civilisation s’étendra sur terre, plus on verra disparaître les guerres et les conquêtes, comme l’esclavage et la misère ». En effet, l’un des grands rêves des Lumières, c’était de croire que la diffusion des connaissances modernes et le progrès scientifique devraient rendre l’espèce humaine meilleure. On sait que cette promesse n’a jamais été tenue. Notre époque connaît un développement technologique fulgurant ; pourtant, les guerres et les conquêtes ne se sont pas arrêtées, la misère n’a pas diminué et même l’esclavage n’a été banni que des règlements, non dans les pratiques. Ainsi, l’explosion de la bombe atomique au-dessus de Hiroshima est à la fois un indice de progrès scientifique et technique, et la preuve d’une régression morale de la civilisation. Pis, comme l’histoire récente l’a montré, les plus grands actes de barbarie n’ont pas été commis par des êtres particulièrement incultes. À l’opposé des illusions entretenues par certains partisans des Lumières, Rousseau, dès son premier écrit, le « Discours sur les sciences et les arts », se sépare de ses amis philosophes et Encyclopédistes, en renonçant à croire que la diffusion des œuvres et des techniques rendra l’humanité meilleure. Loin de contribuer à l’avancement de la morale et à une bienveillance accrue pour les autres, soutient-il, le perfectionnement des sciences et des arts nuit au progrès moral. « Nous pouvons être hommes sans être savants », conclut Rousseau dans « Émile, ou de l’éducation ». Ces exemples renseignent sur la nécessaire séparation entre la recherche elle-même et ses conséquences, positives ou négatives. Le secret de la fission de l’atome a été découvert au sein de la culture occidentale, mais la décision de lâcher la bombe atomique sur quelques centaines de milliers de Japonais y a également été rendue possible, grâce probablement au même mécanisme de fragmentation et de dissociation entre fin et moyens, entre morale et connaissance. Aujourd’hui, l’humanité est confrontée à nouveau à un tournant. Les progrès fulgurants de l’IA générative suscitent autant de promesses que d’inquiétudes. Cet été, les grands patrons de la Tech américaine ont tiré la sonnette d’alarme et appelé à mieux contrôler cette technologie. Les risques d’une IA hors de contrôle sont réels. Certains redoutent même « une extinction de l’humanité ». Le plus inquiétant, c’est que les principaux leaders du monde ne semblent pas avoir pris au sérieux ces mises en garde. En dehors de la prise de position salutaire du pape Léon XIV et du Secrétaire général de l’Onu António Guterres, rares sont les dirigeants politiques qui semblent se préoccuper des conséquences potentielles d’une IA sans contrôle humain. À titre d’exception, on peut citer l’initiative germano-canadienne « pour une IA au service de l’humain ». Pour le reste, les rivalités géopolitiques ont pris le dessus sur la régulation. Donald Trump a rejeté les mises en garde des grands patrons de la Tech américaine, pensant que toute régulation laisserait le champ libre au rival chinois. Or, l’enjeu fondamental aujourd’hui, c’est de parvenir à une gouvernance mondiale de l’IA. La génération précédente avait eu l’intelligence d’accepter de mettre en place des mécanismes pour un contrôle mutuel des armes nucléaires et le Traité de non-prolifération (Tnp). Même sur ce registre, on assiste aujourd’hui à un démantèlement des traités de l’ère guerre-froide qui, malgré leurs limites, avaient le mérite d’éviter une guerre nucléaire dévastatrice pour l’humanité. En définitive, l’IA n’est pas le problème. C’est la crise de la gouvernance mondiale qui inquiète. Et l’Histoire nous a montré que quand les rivalités géopolitiques l’emportent sur la coopération entre grandes puissances, cela ne peut conduire qu’au désastre. seydou.ka@lesoleil.sn

items.title: WADA seeks tough anti-doping stance from Kenya
items.description: Kenya as future hosts of the World Athletics Championship must strive for zero tolerance for drugs in sport, the World Anti Doping Agency (WADA) boss said on Tuesday. Despite a long-running doping crisis, Kenya were last month awarded the 2029 World Athletics Championships, the first time the event will be held in Africa. “Kenya proudly calls itself the Home of Champions. But for that home to remain respected and credible, it must also be clean,” WADA chief Witold Banka said at the end of a three-day visit to the east African country. “That is why Kenya needs a strong culture of clean sport, zero tolerance for doping, and a more determined approach to preventing and fighting doping. “Kenya is a great sporting nation full of great athletes and you become, the more important area of sport when it comes to organising major sporting events. “It’s a big honour for you but it’s a bigger responsibility as well and brings pressure and big requirements from our side as well”, Banka added. Banka said that joint cooperation with Kenyan authorities would help lay the foundations for a cleaner sport. “WADA or ADAK (Anti-Doping Agency of Kenya) alone cannot achieve its vision if we do not cooperate with those who have the power to go against those who are producing, smuggling and trafficking dangerous steroids to your athletes,” he said. “We’ve found a common understanding and we are on the same track and there’s a clear goal within Kenya for zero tolerance for doping policy and it has to be established immediately with joint actions and a more aggressive approach to those who are destroying the image of the country and the reputation of the athletes.” More than 140 Kenyan athletes, mainly long-distance runners, have been suspended by the Athletics Integrity Unit (AIU) since 2017. aik/ea/pb The post WADA seeks tough anti-doping stance from Kenya appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Sebta : 80 % des migrants ont opté pour le retour "volontaire"
items.description: A Sebta occupée, désormais 80 % des migrants évacués du campement d’El Trampolín sont retournés « volontairement » au Maroc, selon la presse ibérique. Ces retours volontaires ont été faits le premier jour de l'opération et l'opération n'aura duré que quelques heures. Alors que les forces de sécurités espagnoles ont procédé à l'évacuation des campements sur la plage Trampolin ce week-end, la majorité des migrants présent sur-place ont choisi la voie du retour volontaire. Parmi les raisons expliquant ce retour de leur propre chef, figure leur situation qui ne semble pas trouver d'issue qui leur sied, la dégradation de leurs conditions de vie ainsi que la météo qui commence à peser lourd sur leur quotidien. Avec l'arrivée de la saison automnale, les baisses de températures se font ressentir encore plus intensément au bord de la plage avec les vents marins humides. Les pluies parfois torrentielles, et les orages annoncés par la météorologie, ont également pesé sur les décisions des migrants qui se sont retrouvés dans des conditions difficilement tolérables dans ces camps de fortune. Selon El Plural, « 900 migrants sur un total de 1 100 sont retournés dans le pays voisin dimanche dernier », ce qui fait que seuls 200 personnes sont restées à Sebta occupée, au niveau du centre d’enregistrement d’El Tarajal. L'agence de presse espagnole Efe, a quant à elle fait état d'un retour de 1200 migrants mardi, citant des sources policières locales. Ces retours volontaires se sont faits dès le premier jour et ont surpris les forces de polices, selon la même source. Elle explique que « la police nationale est arrivée à l'improviste dimanche dernier dans le cadre d'une opération planifiée depuis le milieu de la semaine précédente », en ajoutant qu'à ce moment-là, 2 500 personnes se trouvaient sur la plage, « mais la grande majorité d'entre elles l'avaient quittée en fin de journée ». Le média ajoute que les migrants retournaient à pied au point de passage d'El Tarajal et sortaient par une porte située à gauche du poste de contrôle. Cette porte normalement verrouillée restait ouverte pour permettre aux migrants de quitter la ville, sans escorte militaire ou policière avant de passer le contrôle au niveau des autorités marocaines. Lundi, l'opération d'évacuation des zones occupées par les migrants s'est poursuivie avec un démantèlement complet du campement de la plage Trampolin. Certains migrants ont pris des bus pour leur enregistrement au niveau du Centre d'Assistance Temporaire aux Étrangers (CATE) . Dans ce centre, les personnes fournissent leurs informations dans l'idée d'entamer les démarches d'immigration avant d'être admises dans un centre d'accueil, sauf leur enregistrement a plus de 90% de chances d'être conclu par une procédure d'expulsion, d'où le choix du retour volontaire. « La situation rappelle celle observée quelques jours auparavant, lorsque plus de 150 migrants présents sur la plage de Benítez avaient également choisi de retourner au Maroc », a indiqué Efe, soulignant qu'il reconnaissaient qu’ils ne remplissaient pas les conditions requises pour demander une protection internationale, seul critère permettant leur transfert vers les centres d’accueil gérés par les autorités locales. « L'intervention n'a duré que quelques heures, durant lesquelles les agents n'ont évacué qu'environ 300 personnes de la plage, dont deux cents sont retournées « volontairement » » , souligne le média. Si la grande majorité des migrants ont choisi le retour volontaire, une infime minorité aurait pris la route pour les montages afin d'éviter d'être déplacés de force, selon la même source citée. Toutefois, il n'est pas possible de déterminer si la direction prise vers la montagne avait pour but de rester à Sebta ou de quitter les lieux sans escorte policière. The post Sebta : 80 % des migrants ont opté pour le retour "volontaire" appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Le Ter ? Il n’a pas fallu attendre dix ans (Par Elhadj Ibrahima THIAM)
items.description: «Le Ter, dans dix ans, vous m’en direz des nouvelles ». C’était le titre d’une chronique que nous avions consacrée, dans ces mêmes pages, aux polémiques qui accompagnaient l’arrivée du Train express régional. Nous étions au début de 2019. Le coût, le tracé, la pertinence, l’utilité : tout avait été passé au crible. Et parfois avec beaucoup de passion. Nous n’en sommes pas encore à dix ans. Il aura fallu bien moins de temps pour que les nouvelles arrivent. Elles sautent aujourd’hui aux yeux de tout le monde. Même de certains contempteurs d’hier. Qui peut douter, aujourd’hui, que le Ter fait désormais partie du quotidien de milliers de Sénégalais ? Il suffit de se rendre dans les gares aux heures de pointe pour s’en convaincre. Des centaines de voyageurs s’y pressent chaque jour. Pour beaucoup, le Ter représente un gain de temps, davantage de confort et une certaine régularité dans les déplacements. Ces usagers n’ont pas besoin de longs discours pour mesurer ce que le train a changé dans leur quotidien. C’est peut-être là que se trouve la meilleure réponse aux polémiques d’hier : dans l’usage. Et la semaine passée, le Ter a franchi une nouvelle étape. Il ne s’arrête plus à Diamniadio. Il poursuit désormais son trajet jusqu’à l’Aéroport international Blaise-Diagne de Diass (Aibd). En attendant son prolongement vers Thiès, et peut-être au-delà. La liaison peut sembler naturelle. Dans de nombreux pays, le train dessert directement les aéroports et permet aux voyageurs de rejoindre les terminaux sans dépendre des aléas de la circulation. Pour le Sénégal, elle marque surtout une nouvelle halte dans l’histoire d’un projet qui, sept ans après son lancement, a fini par entrer dans les habitudes. Le Ter n’est malheureusement pas le seul grand projet de transport à avoir connu un tel parcours. Le Bus rapid transit (Brt), l’autoroute à péage Dakar-Diamniadio ou encore l’autoroute Ila Touba ont eux aussi suscité leur lot de critiques. À chaque fois, la même question revenait : avions-nous réellement besoin de ces infrastructures ? Était-il pertinent d’y consacrer autant d’argent ? Cela ne signifie pas que ces projets sont exempts de critiques ni que toutes les interrogations soulevées à leur lancement étaient infondées. Mais le temps permet parfois de regarder une infrastructure autrement que dans le seul bruit de son inauguration. Dakar grandit. Sa population augmente, son parc automobile aussi, et les déplacements deviennent chaque année plus nombreux et plus complexes. La capitale concentre une part importante de la population et de l’activité économique du pays sur un territoire réduit. Une grande partie du parc automobile y circule également. Dans ces conditions, construire toujours plus de routes ne peut constituer, à lui seul, une réponse durable. L’enjeu est aussi de diversifier les modes de transport et de développer des solutions collectives capables d’absorber une part croissante des déplacements. Le Ter et le Brt doivent donc être regardés dans cette perspective. Ils ne sont pas seulement des réponses aux difficultés d’aujourd’hui. Ils participent aussi à la préparation de la ville de demain. Mais une chose est certaine : le Ter n’est plus seulement un projet dont on parle. Il est devenu une infrastructure que l’on utilise. S’il faut encore quelques années pour mesurer pleinement son impact sur la mobilité et l’organisation du territoire, son prolongement jusqu’à l’aéroport a le mérite de rappeler que certaines infrastructures prennent tout leur sens avec le temps, à mesure que les besoins évoluent et que les usages se développent. Au fond, il n’aura pas fallu attendre dix ans pour avoir des nouvelles du Ter. elhadjibrahima.thiam@lesoleil.sn

items.title: ‘2026 is the new 1789’: French students take school anger to Paris streets
items.description: As drums pounded and chants rang out, 16-year-old Yanis, flanked by a knot of friends, rattled off why he had joined tens of thousands surging through the streets of Paris on Tuesday to demand better learning conditions. “There are no toilets, no toilet paper, everything is broken,” he said, his schoolmates nodding and chiming in. “We go to class from 8:00 am to 6:00 pm with a one-hour break.” “There are 36 of us in class. We can’t study,” the teenager from the northern Paris suburb of Sarcelles told AFP, calling conditions at his high school “unacceptable”. He was among some 56,000 people who poured onto the streets of Paris on Tuesday as part of a protest movement that began in late September. Across France, students and teachers have blocked the entrances to hundreds of high schools for 15- to 17-year-olds, protesting against teacher shortages, overloaded timetables, ill-equipped classrooms and buildings not designed to cope with rising temperatures. On Tuesday, protesters flooded into the Place de la Republique in central Paris, hoisting signs. “2026 is the new 1789,” declared one, a nod to the French Revolution. Another placard took the form of an oversized middle finger. The scent of merguez sausages — a fixture of French demonstrations — drifted through the square. Demonstrators danced and clapped to pounding drums, breaking into chants calling for President Emmanuel Macron to resign and denouncing the far right ahead of presidential elections next year. – ‘I don’t have a future’ – But beneath the festive atmosphere, some of the young protesters struck a bleaker note. Fidele, 15, who had come with Yanis, dreamt of becoming a lawyer but said conditions at his school had left him pessimistic about whether he could get there. “When I see the system, I tell myself that I don’t have a future” in this country, he said. Nearby, 16-year-old Noham had his sights set on becoming a computer engineer, but worried that overcrowded classrooms and teacher shortages were putting that ambition out of reach. “Without access to an education, I can’t have the job I dream of,” he said. “It’s an enormous amount of stress.” Nadine Zilliacus, an educator for 20 years, said she had seen the same disillusionment take hold among even younger pupils, who increasingly expressed a “really dark” view of what lies ahead. “We tell them you have to prepare for the future with a job you like,” she said. “Even in middle school they tell us: ‘There’s no point, anyway we won’t have jobs’.” – ‘We’re neglected’ – Further along the route, the crowd pressed towards the march’s endpoint, clapping and chanting before voices swelled into a rendition of the Marseillaise, France’s national anthem. From a balcony overhead, a silver-haired woman leaned out to encourage the protesters below. Spotting her, the crowd turned their faces upwards and broke into chants of “Mamie! Mamie!” — an affectionate French term for grandmother. Among those making their way through the crowd was Ami, 17, who had travelled into Paris with a group of friends to protest against conditions at her high school in the city’s suburbs. “Compared with schools in central Paris, we’re neglected,” she said. As the march reached the Nation roundabout, the festive mood began to shift, with police carrying riot shields barring the route and some protesters throwing stones at the officers. As Ami and her friends drew closer, the boom of tear gas canisters fired by police cut through the singing. The girls screamed and stopped in their tracks, unsure whether to keep moving forward. Nearby, a middle-aged woman had mascara streaking down her face after being caught in the tear gas, while a young man comforted her. Ami said she did not understand the police response. “We’re just protesting, we’re singing, and that’s all,” she said, adding that she was scared. After a day of drums, chants and dancing through the capital, she was ready to leave. “We just want to go home,” she said. ekf/ah/gv The post ‘2026 is the new 1789’: French students take school anger to Paris streets appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Accès universel à l’électricité : 998 milliards de FCFA d’engagements pour l’objectif 2029
items.description: Le Sénégal entend accélérer la réalisation de l’accès universel à l’électricité à l’horizon 2029. À cet effet, le ministère de l’Énergie et du Pétrole a réuni, mardi 6 octobre 2026, ses partenaires techniques et financiers ainsi que les acteurs du secteur privé autour d’une table ronde consacrée à la mobilisation des financements. Les engagements annoncés à cette occasion atteignent 998 milliards de FCFA, dépassant largement les besoins estimés. Sous la vision du président de la République, Bassirou Diomaye Diakhar Faye, le gouvernement veut franchir une nouvelle étape dans la politique d’électrification du pays. Le ministre de l’Énergie et du Pétrole, El Hadji Abdourahmane Diouf, a co-présidé, avec le ministre de l’Économie, des Finances et du Plan, Cheikh Diba, une table ronde consacrée à l’accélération de l’accès universel à l’électricité. L’objectif affiché est de garantir l’accès à l’électricité à chaque Sénégalais à l’horizon 2029. Une ambition qui nécessite d’intensifier les investissements, notamment dans les zones encore non desservies. Selon les données présentées par le ministère, le taux national d’accès à l’électricité s’établissait à 86,2 % à fin 2024. Sur les 25 725 localités recensées au Sénégal, 12 683 sont déjà électrifiées, tandis que 6 571 sont couvertes par des projets en cours de réalisation. Il reste ainsi 6 471 localités à couvrir, soit près d’un million de Sénégalais. Pour franchir cette dernière étape, les besoins financiers étaient initialement estimés à près de 400 milliards de FCFA. Des engagements largement supérieurs aux besoins La table ronde a permis d’enregistrer des engagements financiers importants de la part des différents partenaires. Au titre des partenaires techniques et financiers, 181 milliards de FCFA ont été annoncés pour la réalisation de nouveaux projets d’électrification. Le secteur privé s’est également fortement mobilisé, avec des engagements annoncés à hauteur de 817 milliards de FCFA. Au total, 998 milliards de FCFA font ainsi l’objet d’engagements, soit un montant largement supérieur aux besoins estimés pour assurer la couverture des localités restantes. À ces engagements s’ajoutent plusieurs offres du secteur privé reçues en ligne, qui devraient contribuer à renforcer davantage les capacités de financement des projets d’électrification. Pour le gouvernement, cette mobilisation traduit l’intérêt des partenaires techniques et financiers et des investisseurs privés pour l’ambition sénégalaise en matière d’accès universel à l’électricité. Une priorité pour l’équité territoriale Au-delà des infrastructures électriques, l’accès universel est présenté comme un levier de justice sociale, d’équité territoriale et de transformation économique. La couverture des localités encore dépourvues d’électricité doit notamment permettre d’améliorer les conditions de vie des populations et de favoriser le développement des activités économiques dans les territoires. Avec les engagements annoncés lors de cette table ronde, le Sénégal dispose désormais d’une marge financière importante pour accélérer ses projets et se rapprocher de son objectif d’un accès universel à l’électricité en 2029. C.G.D

items.title: Benue govt, PDP clash over threat to pull down billboards
items.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi The Benue State Government and the opposition Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) have sharply disagreed over the planned removal of unauthorised billboards across the state, with the PDP alleging the exercise was politically motivated and targeted opposition campaign materials ahead of the 2027 governorship election. The state government, through the Benue State Signage and Advertisement Agency, Benue State Internal Revenue Service, BIRS, and the Urban Development Board, had on Tuesday issued a two-week ultimatum to owners and operators of unauthorised billboards to regularise them or face removal. The directive, contained in a statement signed by the Commissioner for Information and Orientation, Chief Solomon Iorpev, said enforcement would commence on October 20, 2026, with the removal of every billboard that had not been regularised. But the PDP, through its State Publicity Secretary, Bright Antyo, described the directive as “a desperate, anti-democratic and politically motivated attempt to cripple opposition campaigns ahead of the 2027 governorship election.” The party urged the state government to abandon what it described as an attempt to intimidate political opponents and monopolise public spaces. Explaining the government’s position, Iorpev said the relevant agencies had “observed with concern the arbitrary erection of billboards across the State by individuals, groups and political parties.” According to him, “These structures have been put up without a permit from the Signage and Advertisement Agency, without clearance from the Urban Development Board, and without payment of the prescribed fees.” “This practice breaches the law. It deprives the State of legitimate revenue, endangers public safety, and undermines the orderly development of our towns and cities,” he added. The government, however, said it was giving billboard owners the opportunity to comply rather than immediately commence enforcement. Iorpev explained that the authorities were “prepared to assume that many of those responsible acted out of ignorance of the law and not out of deliberate defiance. For this reason, the Agencies are giving everyone who has erected a billboard a grace period of two weeks, beginning today, Tuesday, 6th October 2026,” he said. The commissioner urged owners and operators of unauthorised billboards to use the period to “retrace their steps and do the right thing” by approaching the Benue State Signage and Advertisement Agency to begin the permit process, obtain clearance from the Urban Development Board, and pay all required fees. He warned that the deadline would not be extended saying “Let it be clear that there will not be another notice before enforcement which will commence on Tuesday, 20th October 2026. The enforcement teams are expected to begin removing every billboard that has not been regularised from the set date. Billboards taken down will be at the owners’ cost, and no further notice will be given. “Anyone who ignores this window should expect no sympathy and no exception, regardless of status, affiliation or political party. We are a law-abiding people, and we believe every Benue citizen wants to do the right thing. This grace period is a sign of the Government’s goodwill and of its preference for compliance over confrontation. We urge all concerned to make use of it,” the commissioner stated. However, the PDP rejected the government’s explanation, arguing that the timing of the directive suggested a political motive. In its reaction signed by Antyo, the opposition party said it had “noted with alarm the directive issued by the Benue State Government threatening to commence the removal of billboards and posters across the state from October 20, 2026.” The PDP said it “condemns this action in the strongest possible terms” and described it as “a desperate, anti-democratic and politically motivated attempt to cripple opposition campaigns ahead of the 2027 governorship election.” According to the party, opposition billboards carrying “messages of hope, security, economic revival and political change” had recently appeared in major towns and communities across the state. It alleged that rather than address issues raised by residents, Governor Hyacinth Alia’s administration was attempting to intimidate political opponents. “The sudden two-week ultimatum issued by the government is not a coincidence. It bears all the markings of a calculated operation aimed at clearing public spaces of opposition campaign materials and restricting the visibility of alternative political voices as the 2027 election approaches,” the PDP alleged. The party questioned the timing and manner of the government’s proposed enforcement saying, “If the Alia administration was genuinely interested in enforcing signage laws, why did it wait until now? “Why were these regulations not vigorously enforced before opposition campaigns began gaining traction? Why has the government suddenly become eager to dismantle structures carrying messages that challenge its record?” the PDP asked. The PDP claimed the directive targeted political opponents, alleging that the administration was unsettled by what it described as growing dissatisfaction with the government and increasing acceptance of alternative political options ahead of the 2027 election. The party further alleged that government institutions could be deployed against political opponents, describing the directive as “draconian, vindictive and dangerous for democracy.” It said: “It creates the impression that government agencies are being mobilised, not for public service, but as instruments of political warfare against perceived opponents.” The opposition party also warned the governor against what it described as an attempt to restrict political competition. “Benue State is not a monarchy, and Governor Alia is not the only candidate who will participate in the 2027 election. The people have a constitutional right to hear different voices, evaluate competing visions and make informed choices at the ballot box.” The PDP argued that political contests should be determined by public confidence and performance, not by the visibility or removal of campaign materials. “We remind the Governor that democracy is not sustained by pulling down opponents’ billboards and posters. Democracy is sustained by winning the trust of the people through good governance, accountability, transparency and tangible results.” The party also used the controversy to raise several issues it said were confronting the state, including insecurity, the condition of Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs), abandoned projects, debt, infrastructure and the economic situation. “Today, Benue people are asking hard questions about insecurity, the plight of IDPs abandoned projects, mounting debt, neglect of 22 local governments, deteriorating rural infrastructure and the worsening economic situation. Destroying opposition campaign materials will not make these questions disappear,” the PDP said. The party therefore warned that “any selective removal of opposition campaign materials under the guise of enforcement will be interpreted as a direct attack on democratic freedoms and a dangerous abuse of state institutions for partisan purposes.” It called on civil society organisations, election observers, the media, security agencies and other stakeholders to monitor the implementation of the directive. “We call on civil society organisations, election observers, the media, security agencies and all defenders of democracy to closely monitor the excesses of Governor Alia and his administration and ensure that no government agency is used as a tool for political persecution,” the party said. The PDP urged the state government to reverse course, saying, “The Governor must abandon this path of political intolerance. Any attempt to intimidate opponents, monopolise public space and create the illusion of an unchallenged political landscape will fail because democracy belongs to the people, not to those temporarily entrusted with power. “Benue belongs to all the people. The democratic space belongs to everyone. No government has the right to reserve it for itself,” it stated. The post Benue govt, PDP clash over threat to pull down billboards appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Team Volta wins NPA 2026 Staff Welfare Week Quiz
items.description: Team Volta has won the National Petroleum Authority’s (NPA) 2026 Staff Welfare Week Quiz Competition after an impressive performance in a keenly contested event involving teams from across the Authority. Each competing team was formed by pairing one of the NPA’s nine operational regions with designated directorates or departments of the Authority. The format was designed to promote collaboration, knowledge sharing and teamwork between the regional offices and head office functions. The quiz was part of activities marking the Authority’s week-long Staff Welfare Celebration, held under the theme “Our People, Our Teamwork and the Spirit That Makes NPA One Family.” Contestants were tested on the NPA’s legal and regulatory mandate, the functions of the Authority’s technical directorates, Ghana’s Green Transition Plan, downstream petroleum policy, developments in the global oil and gas industry, and current affairs. Professor Elsie Effah Kaufmann, Quiz Mistress of the National Science and Maths Quiz (NSMQ), was the Special Guest, while Dr Riverson Oppong of the Chamber of Oil Marketing Companies (COMAC) served as Quiz Master. Team Volta takes top prize Team Volta, made up of the Volta Regional Office, the Risk Directorate and the Consumer Services Directorate, won the competition and received a cash prize of GH¢30,000. The team was represented on stage by three contestants: Seth Doe of IM&HSE at the Volta Regional Office, Emmanuel Ketsi of the Consumer Services Directorate, and Ransford Ansah of the Risk Directorate. Team Bono, made up of the Bono Regional Office, the Gas Directorate, the Administration and Insurance Directorate, and the CEO Secretariat, placed second and received GH¢20,000. Team Western, made up of the Western Regional Office and the Security and Intelligence Directorate, finished third and received GH¢10,000. Teamwork and preparation The Volta Regional Manager of the NPA, Mr Prospero Kojo Cyriaano, congratulated Team Volta and commended its members for the discipline and preparation they showed throughout the competition. He encouraged staff to keep deepening their understanding of the downstream petroleum industry, noting that strong industry knowledge is essential to the effective discharge of the Authority’s regulatory mandate. The Director of Risk, Mr Joseph Awan, said Team Volta’s success showed the value of collaboration across the Authority’s functional areas. “Team Volta brought together colleagues from the regional office, Risk and Consumer Services, each contributing different perspectives and expertise. Their success shows the value of collaboration and knowledge sharing across the Authority as we work collectively to deliver on our regulatory mandate,” he said. The Director of Consumer Services, Mrs Eunice Budu Nyarko, also congratulated the team. She commended Ing. Johnson Gbagbo Jnr, Head of Department in the Consumer Services Directorate, and Mr Patrick Sam, Head of Department in the Risk Directorate, for their commitment to preparing the team. She urged staff to continue building their knowledge of the Authority and the downstream petroleum industry as part of their professional development. The 2026 Staff Welfare Week Quiz Competition was held at the Moses Asaga Auditorium of the National Petroleum Authority.

items.title: Team Eternity Ghana releases new album “The Promise – Phase 1”
items.description: Ghanaian gospel music collective, Team Eternity Ghana (TEG), announces the release of the first phase of their highly anticipated new album, “The Promise.” The album is anchored on God’s word of promise in Genesis 28:15. “I am with thee… I will not leave thee, until I have done that which I have spoken to thee of.” Genesis 28:15. For Team Eternity Ghana, “The Promise” is more than an album. It is a divine assignment of covenant entrusted to the collective and a message of assurance to a generation navigating uncertainty, disappointment, and the need for hope. The album centers on three foundational truths: His Presence, His Attention, and His Protection , reminding listeners that God is with them, hears their prayers, and remains their refuge and deliverer. Musically, “The Promise” brings together a contemporary gospel sound designed to connect across generations, speaking to Millennials, Gen Z, and the emerging Gen Alpha audience. The project carries songs of hope, restoration, faith and blessed assurance, with the intention of doing more than entertaining listeners — it seeks to point them back to the faithfulness of God. The album arrives during a significant year for Team Eternity Ghana, as the collective marks 13 years since its formation. Over the past few years, TEG has released two albums and an EP, with fan favourites including “Dede Defe,” “My Reason,” and “Brass Band Medley.” The group has also received recognition at the 2025 Ghana Praise Achievement Awards, for Artist of the Year and Best Group of the Year. The collective at the 2025 Telecel Ghana Music Awards were also awarded “Best Group of the Year.” With “The Promise” album, Team Eternity Ghana enters a new chapter while holding firmly to the message that has shaped its journey: God keeps His word. As the group releases the first installment of “The Promise” album, TEG invites listeners from all over the world to experience a refreshing sound of hope, restoration, and assurance.

items.title: Rival clubs demand title stripping, transfer bans for Man City
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Rival Premier League clubs are calling for Manchester City to face a range of punishments, including title stripping and transfer bans, if the club’s appeal against its financial breaches verdict fails, according to the BBC. An independent commission found Manchester City guilty of all charges relating to breaches of the Premier League’s financial regulations between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons. City have appealed against the verdict. However, sources told BBC Sport that a number of Premier League clubs want any eventual sanctions to cover both the period in which the breaches occurred and City’s future participation in the competition. There is also a feeling in at least four Premier League boardrooms that a single points deduction resulting in relegation to the Championship would not be sufficient punishment given the scale of the findings. One senior club source said City should be stripped of the titles they won during the period covered by the verdict. The source added that there was “no great rush” among clubs to redistribute the trophies, but rather to take the honours away and leave them vacant. The source warned that the credibility of the Premier League would be undermined if City were allowed to retain the eight major trophies they won during the period in which they were found guilty of the breaches. However, BBC Sport said it had previously been told there was little appetite among some other clubs for City to be stripped of their titles, highlighting the differing views across the league. On future sanctions, some Premier League figures believe a points deduction imposed in only one season would amount to a “bump in the road” for City, given the likelihood of the club returning to the top flight at the first opportunity. As a result, some clubs believe any points deduction should be spread over multiple seasons. There is also support in some quarters for transfer bans covering several windows, which could make it harder for City to rebuild and return to the Premier League quickly if they are relegated. One club source described it as “bizarre, almost obtuse” if City were allowed to operate in the January transfer window while the process remained ongoing and sanctions had yet to be imposed. Another proposal being discussed is a “tariff-based system”, under which City’s past league finishing positions could be adjusted through a points deduction. Rival clubs could then receive compensation from City based on where they would have finished compared with their actual positions. City have consistently maintained their innocence and are challenging the independent commission’s findings through an appeal. Meanwhile, BBC Sport understands City manager Enzo Maresca will address his players collectively after they return from international duty on Thursday, ahead of Sunday’s Premier League meeting with Liverpool at Anfield. The match will be City’s first since the verdict became public. Merseyside Police said it had received queries about the fixture and confirmed it would have “an appropriate policing operation in place on the day”. Liverpool sources told BBC Sport the club was treating the fixture as “business as usual”, with no additional measures planned. One source said supporters had “the right to express their feelings” but hoped they would not overstep the mark. items.title: N100bn Audit Query: Reps give FCT area councils seven-day final ultimatum
items.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina,Abuja The House of Representatives Public Accounts Committee (PAC) has issued a seven-day final summons to officials of the six Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Area Councils over outstanding audit queries involving about N100 billion. The committee’s action followed the failure of the six Area Council chairmen to honour its invitation to appear and respond to financial queries contained in the Auditor-General’s reports. The affected councils are Abaji, Abuja Municipal Area Council (AMAC), Bwari, Gwagwalada, Kuje and Kwali. The chairmen had requested September 22, 2026, as the date for their appearance, but failed to attend the sitting or send representatives. Consequently, the committee summoned the Directors of Personnel Management and Finance, as well as Heads of Audit of the six councils, to appear before it on October 14, 2026, or face sanctions in line with relevant service rules. Chairman of the PAC, Rep. Bamidele Salam, disclosed this while speaking with journalists in Abuja on Tuesday. Salam said the committee had repeatedly invited the councils to provide explanations and supporting documents needed to resolve the audit queries. “The last date of appearance of the Abuja Area Councils was September 22, 2026, which was a date they requested for and which was graciously granted by the committee. Yet, they failed to appear or send in any representation. “The committee has therefore decided to issue summons to the Directors of Personnel Management and Finance of these local governments, including their Heads of Audit, to appear without fail on Wednesday, October 14, failure of which they will be made to bear consequences according to service rules,” he said. The queries are contained in the Annual Audit Report of the Auditor-General for the Six FCT Area Councils for the year ended December 31, 2021. According to the report, the councils had outstanding liabilities of about N7.65 billion arising from unremitted pension deductions, Pay As You Earn (PAYE), Value Added Tax (VAT), withholding tax and unpaid obligations to contractors. AMAC accounted for the highest liability at N2.19 billion, followed by Bwari with N1.49 billion and Kwali with N1.46 billion. Gwagwalada had N1.01 billion in outstanding liabilities, while Kuje and Abaji had N892.2 million and N593.8 million respectively. The Auditor-General said the liabilities were due for remittance to the Nigeria Revenue Service, FCT Inland Revenue Service, Pension Fund Administrators and contractors. The report also raised concerns over the councils’ management of fixed assets, particularly the failure to properly maintain and update asset registers. Gwagwalada was specifically queried over non-current assets valued at N336 million, whose ledger records, according to the report, were not properly maintained and updated. The Auditor-General warned that the poor record-keeping could create room for assets to be lost without being traced, adding that the lapse was common among the FCT Area Councils. The PAC is also demanding explanations and supporting documents on N24.87 billion spent by the six councils on personnel, overheads and capital expenditure in 2021. AMAC accounted for N5.03 billion, Gwagwalada N4.66 billion, Kuje N3.85 billion, Kwali N3.84 billion, Bwari N3.74 billion and Abaji N3.71 billion. Salam disclosed that the committee had uncovered additional concerns in the audit reports for 2022 and part of 2023, including alleged understatement of Internally Generated Revenue, unauthorised disposal of assets, non-disclosure of statutory revenue and failure to remit withholding tax. He also said the councils had failed to audit and submit their financial accounts for 2023, 2024 and 2025, contrary to statutory requirements. The lawmaker said the committee would insist on transparency and accountability in the management of public resources, stressing that officials found culpable would be held responsible in accordance with the law. items.title: Mali : l’armée reprend Kidal, bastion des rebelles touaregs
items.description: La ville stratégique de Kidal, longtemps occupée par les rebelles touareg, a été reprise, mardi, par l'armée malienne, appuyée par les paramilitaires russes de Africa Corps qui aident Bamako dans sa lutte antiterroriste. Cette reprise est très symbolique pour l'Etat malien en proie à une crise sécuritaire majeure depuis 2012 causée par les groupes terroristes ainsi que les rebelles touaregs. L'armée malienne avait été chassée de Kidal en avril, devenue chef lieu des rebelles. La ville était depuis ce jour, aux mains du Front de libération de l'Azawad (FLA) et ses alliés jihadistes du Groupe de soutien à l'islam et aux musulmans (JNIM), affilié à Al-Qaïda. L'armée malienne a annoncé mardi, avoir lancé des « opérations aéroterrestres d'envergure » dans la région de Kidal notamment pour « de neutraliser les groupes armés terroristes opérant dans toute la région » et restaurer « la sécurité des populations et la libre circulation des personnes et des biens ». Cette annonce a été suivie par un « repli stratégique » de la FLA, qui a avancé l'idée de « préserver » ses capacités humaines et logistiques, en notant qu'il s'agit d'une « mesure opérationnelle temporaire ». Dans un communiqué, le FLA, a indiqué que « face aux risques croissants pesant sur les rares populations civiles encore présentes dans la ville par l'utilisation disproportionnée de vecteurs aériens par les mercenaires russes de l'Africa Corps et (…) la junte militaire de Bamako, le commandement militaire du FLA décide de procéder à un repli stratégique de la localité de Kidal ». Les habitants de la ville ont choisi de quitter les lieux, craignant des affrontements meurtriers. Selon plusieurs témoins, la ville a été désertée et l'armée a pu entrer vers la mi-journée. items.title: Inside the human genome: Why scientists are still discovering who we are
items.description: More than two decades after scientists announced the completion of the first human genome sequence, the human genome continues to yield new insights. The Human Genome Project was a landmark achievement, but scientists soon realized that sequencing the genome was only the beginning. The human genome contains billions of DNA bases, and understanding what they do and how differences between people affect health is an enormous scientific challenge. Modern genomics is now moving beyond simply producing a reference sequence. Researchers are working to create a more complete picture of human genetic diversity by comparing the genomes of people from different ancestral backgrounds. This matters because no single human genome represents everyone. Genetic differences between populations can provide important information about disease, biological adaptation and responses to medicines. A more diverse understanding of the genome could therefore improve the accuracy of genetic research and medical applications. The advances are particularly significant for people living with rare diseases. Some patients spend years undergoing tests without a clear diagnosis. Genome sequencing can sometimes identify genetic variants that explain previously unexplained conditions, providing families with answers and helping doctors understand how to manage a disease. But genomics is also raising new questions about privacy. A person’s genome contains uniquely personal information, and some genetic information can also reveal clues about biological relatives. Protecting genomic data is therefore an increasingly important responsibility for researchers, hospitals and governments. There is another challenge: representation. If genomic research does not adequately represent global populations, the benefits of genomic medicine may be distributed unequally. Scientists increasingly recognise that understanding humanity’s genetic diversity requires participation by communities around the world. The next chapter of genomics will therefore not simply be about sequencing DNA more quickly. It will be about understanding the enormous diversity of the human genome and ensuring that scientific discoveries benefit the people whose genetic information makes them possible. The genome may be encoded in DNA, but people will shape its future.

items.title: UEFA monitoring Man City’s 115-charge case, considers action after appeal
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye UEFA is monitoring Manchester City’s financial-rule case and will wait until the end of the Premier League’s disciplinary process before considering any potential action against Manchester City, Sky Sports reports. Manchester City were found guilty by an independent commission of serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules between 2009 and 2018, including five charges relating to breaches of UEFA’s Financial Fair Play rules. City have appealed the verdict and continue to deny any wrongdoing, insisting that they have a “comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence” to support their position. According to Sky Sports chief correspondent Kaveh Solhekol, UEFA is monitoring developments and will wait until the Premier League disciplinary process is completed before deciding whether to take any potential action against City. The independent commission found that City’s owners had put £830 million into the club, which was disguised as sponsorship income over nine seasons. The commission also found City significantly breached both Premier League and UEFA spending limits and broke “well over 100” Premier League regulations. UEFA previously took action against City over Financial Fair Play breaches. In 2014, the club agreed a settlement with UEFA which included a £49 million fine, of which £32 million was suspended. In 2020, UEFA found City guilty of breaching its Financial Fair Play rules, imposing a €30 million fine and a two-year ban from European competitions. City appealed to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS), which overturned the European competition ban, ruling that UEFA had not established that the club’s owners had disguised equity funding as sponsorship contributions. Other alleged breaches were found to be time-barred. CAS subsequently reduced the fine to €10 million for City’s failure to cooperate with UEFA’s investigation. UEFA’s statute of limitations for financial-rule breaches is five years, while the Premier League has no such limitation, according to Sky Sports. The Premier League’s independent commission, which had access to evidence unavailable to UEFA during its investigation, found City guilty of serious financial breaches spanning nine seasons. City lodged its appeal on October 1 and maintains that the commission’s decision contains “clear material errors, of law, principle and fact” and is “unsafe.” Under the Premier League’s new appeal rules, the process is expected to be concluded within 12 weeks, although City could argue that the new rules should not apply because the case began before they were introduced. Sky Sports reports that such an argument could potentially push the appeal process into 2027. PAC grills Central Regional Coordinating Council over GH¢14.9m payments processed outside GIFMIS
items.description: The Public Accounts Committee (PAC) has questioned the Central Regional Coordinating Council over payment vouchers totalling GH¢14.88 million that were processed outside the Ghana Integrated Financial Management Information System (GIFMIS). The Committee has warned the council that if the same breach is identified in a subsequent audit, it will regard it as evidence that the institution failed to implement the corrective measures it said it had introduced. The issue came up at the Committee’s sitting on Tuesday, October 6, 2026, when it considered the Auditor-General’s 2025 report on Ministries, Departments and other Agencies. According to the audit finding presented to the Committee, the Central Regional Coordinating Council failed to process payment vouchers totalling GH¢14,882,540.98 through GIFMIS. A representative of the Ministry of Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs told the Committee that the transactions involved donor funds and were subsequently captured through journal vouchers. He said subsequent transactions had been processed through GIFMIS after the audit observation was raised. The explanation prompted further questions from the Committee about why the transactions had initially been processed outside the system. A Committee member questioned whether the fact that the funds were donor-funded justified their exclusion from GIFMIS, stressing that donor funds were still public funds. The representative later explained that the funds formed part of the approved budget and that the donor components had been captured during the budget process. He said the problem arose because, when the releases were made, there was an issue with the budget code required to process the transactions through GIFMIS. According to him, journal vouchers were subsequently raised to capture the transactions on the system and ensure that the accounts accurately reflected the expenditure. The Committee continued to question the representative over the reasons the transactions had not initially been processed through GIFMIS. The Chairperson of the Committee, Abena Osei-Asare, said the concern was not only about the transactions already identified but also whether the system had since been corrected. She warned that if the same problem appeared in a future audit, the Committee would regard it as evidence that the institution had failed to implement the corrective system it claimed to have introduced. “If we find this, then clearly we will know that you failed to learn or you failed to implement the system that you are telling us you have implemented,” she said. The warning followed the Chairperson’s position at the opening of the 2025 audit hearings that institutions must show what had changed after previous audit findings instead of repeatedly appearing before the Committee with explanations for the same weaknesses. She said the Committee would distinguish between administrative infractions and actual financial losses, while requiring institutions to show whether audit recommendations had been implemented and weak systems corrected. The representative of the Central Regional Coordinating Council maintained that subsequent transactions had been processed through GIFMIS and that journal vouchers had been used to capture the earlier transactions that had not gone through the system.

items.title: Insecurity: Armed men ambush commercial vehicle, kill driver in Benue
items.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi A commercial driver, Igba Agenewe, has been killed by suspected armed men while three soldiers travelling in his vehicle were reportedly abducted along the Anyiin-Ayilamo road in Logo Local Government Area (LGA), of Benue State. Agenewe, a member of the National Union of Road Transport Workers, NURTW, Wurukum branch, Anyiin section, was reportedly returning to Makurdi from Anyiin when the gunmen emerged from the bush and opened fire on his vehicle. The incident, which occurred on Monday, has thrown members of the union and the deceased’s colleagues into mourning. Agenewe, who operated from the Wurukum Park in Makurdi, had earlier driven his Sharon bus to Anyiin town with passengers. According to a member of the union, Iorember Tser, the deceased was warned against returning to Makurdi through Ayilamo because of the worsening security situation on the route. Tser said, “When he got to Anyiin, he wanted to return to Makurdi. Some drivers told him that the road was not safe because of the prolonged suspected herders-farmers crisis in Ayilamo, which is a 10-minute drive from Anyiin. He however, insisted on returning to Makurdi, saying, ‘I just passed through the road.’ It was gathered that Agenewe subsequently picked up three passengers said to be military personnel and headed towards Makurdi. However, “when he passed a town called Akwana heading towards Ayilamo, unknown gunmen emerged from the bush and shot him. He died on the spot. The three soldiers were abducted but later regained freedom and returned to Anyiin.” He said the incident has heightened concerns about the safety of motorists and commuters using the Abinsi-Tyulen-Anyiin-Wukari road, particularly the Ayilamo axis, which has seen security challenges linked to the prolonged conflict in the area. The owner of the Sharon bus, Mr Aondona Tyulen, described the killing of his driver as unfortunate and appealed to security agencies to apprehend the perpetrators. Tyulen called on the authorities to intensify security operations in the area and ensure that those responsible for the killing were brought to justice. The remains of Agenewe had, as of the time of filing this report, been deposited at the Ayilamo mortuary. Efforts to obtain a reaction from the Benue State Police Command were unsuccessful, as the Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Peter Aondongu, had not responded to enquiries on the incident as of press time. items.title: 2027: ‘You can’t contest without structure’ – Sowunmi tells Peter Obi
items.description: The convener of The Alternative movement, Segun Sowunmi, has said Peter Obi cannot successfully contest the 2027 presidential election alone, arguing that the contest requires a strong political structure. Sowunmi stated this during an interview on News Central on Tuesday while responding to a question on whether he considered Obi, the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, a threat ahead of the 2027 election. He said political actors must recognise the importance of alliances and political structures when preparing for a presidential contest. “As for Peter, there are seasons and there are times you have to know you are not going to singularly run into an election that requires structure, and you are not going to pretend that you’re not smelling the coffee,” Sowunmi said. He argued that Obi should also consider the political position of governors in the South-East and the benefits their states were receiving from the Federal Government. “If you have five governors in your zone, which is the South-East zone, and all of them are saying, from what we can see, from the resources we’re getting, from the construction that is going on, from the integration, let’s keep it there. Maybe you are good to think it that way,” he said. Sowunmi also cited the Federal Government’s infrastructure projects in the South-East, particularly the work of the Minister of Works, as a factor that could influence political calculations in the region. “If you see your Minister of Works doing exceedingly more than anybody since the Civil War to return infrastructure to the South-East, you may say, ‘Okay, why not?” he said. The former PDP chieftain, however, said nobody should be prevented from contesting an election, even where such a candidate may not have sufficient political structure to win. “But nobody has the right to force anybody not to go into the field to lose an election,” he said. Sowunmi also advocated political cooperation among regions, saying the South should collaborate while the incumbent completes his term, after which political power could rotate. “Now that it’s in the South, let the South collaborate together, and let the man that is on the seat finish his term, and let it swing to the North then it will swing back, and there will be opportunities for this negotiation and recalibration,” he said. He added that democracy required contestants, winners and losers, urging candidates who lose elections to accept the outcomes. “Democracy needs somebody to lose. That’s why you need people to also contest elections. So the winner will win, and the losers will lose,” Sowunmi said.
